07Chapter 7 · Dimensionality Reduction

Dimensionality Reduction

Kai ML problems mein har training instance ke hazaaron ya lakhs features hote hain. Itne features training ko slow kar dete hain aur achha solution dhoondhna mushkil kar dete hain — isi problem ko curse of dimensionality kehte hain. Dimensionality reduction iska ilaaj hai.

Curse of dimensionality kya hai?

High-dimensional space mein hamari intuition fail ho jati hai. Ek unit square mein random point ke border ke bahut kareeb hone ki probability sirf 0.4% hoti hai, par 10,000-dimensional hypercube mein ye 99.999999% se zyada ho jati hai — zyada tar points border ke kareeb hote hain. Do random points ke beech average distance 2D mein lagbhag 0.52, 3D mein 0.66, aur 1,000,000 dimensions mein lagbhag 408.25 ho jati hai! Isliye high-dimensional datasets bahut sparse hote hain: training instances ek dusre se bahut door hote hain, distance-based methods (jaise k-nearest neighbors) kam effective ho jate hain, aur naye instances par predictions unreliable ho jati hain. Ek given density ke liye chahiye training instances ki sankhya dimensions ke saath exponentially badhti hai — sirf 100 features ke liye bhi observable universe ke atoms se zyada instances chahiye hote.

Dimensionality reduction se kya fayda?

  • Training tez hoti hai aur model ki performance bhi sudhar sakti hai.
  • Visualization: dimensions ko 2 ya 3 tak kam karke data ko graph par plot kiya ja sakta hai — clusters jaise patterns dikhne lagte hain.
  • Redundancy hatana: MNIST mein border ke pixels lagbhag hamesha white hote hain, aur aas-paas ke pixels highly correlated hote hain — inko drop ya merge karne se zyada information loss nahi hota.

Dhyan rakho — nuksaan bhi hai

Dimensionality kam karne se useful information bhi kho sakti hai, jaise image ko JPEG compress karne se quality girti hai. System thoda worse perform kar sakta hai, khaas taur par agar dimensionality bahut zyada kam kar di. Neural networks jaise kuch models high-dimensional data ko efficiently handle kar lete hain aur khud hi useful information preserve karte hue dimensionality kam kar lete hain. Isliye extra preprocessing step hamesha madad nahi karta.

Do main approaches

  • Projection: training instances ek lower-dimensional subspace ke kareeb hote hain; unko us subspace par project kar do. Jaise 3D data jo ek plane ke kareeb hai, use 2D plane par project karna.
  • Manifold learning: jab subspace twist ho — jaise Swiss roll dataset — to sirf projection se layers squash ho jati hain. Manifold learning us twisted shape ko unroll karta hai. Iske peeche manifold assumption hai: zyada tar real-world high-dimensional datasets ek bahut lower-dimensional manifold ke kareeb hote hain.

Manifold assumption ke saath ek aur implicit assumption hoti hai: ki task lower-dimensional space mein simpler hoga. Ye hamesha sahi nahi hota — kabhi decision boundary original space mein simple hoti hai aur unrolled space mein complex. Dimensionality reduction tab sabse effective hota hai jab dataset features ke muqable chhota ho, noisy ho, ya features highly correlated hon.

Yaad rakho: Is chapter mein hum teen popular techniques dekhenge — PCA, random projection aur LLE — aur phir MDS, Isomap, t-SNE aur LDA jaise aur techniques par ek nazar dalenge.

07.1Chapter 7 · Dimensionality Reduction

PCA — Variance, Components, Compression

Principal component analysis (PCA) sabse popular dimensionality reduction algorithm hai. Ye pehle wo hyperplane dhoondhta hai jo data ke sabse kareeb ho, phir data ko us par project kar deta hai — aur wo bhi is tarah ki maximum variance preserve ho.

Maximum variance kyun?

Jis axis par projection sabse zyada variance preserve kare, wo sabse kam information khota hai. Ye axis wohi hai jo original dataset aur uske projection ke beech mean squared distance ko minimize karta hai. Simple idea hai — aur ye 1901 se chali aa rahi hai!

Principal components kya hote hain?

PCA pehle wo axis dhoondhta hai jo sabse zyada variance account karta hai — ye first principal component (PC) hai. Phir uske orthogonal doosra axis, jo bache hue variance mein sabse zyada account kare — second PC. Aise hi aage, jitne dimensions hain utne PCs. Inko dhoondhne ke liye singular value decomposition (SVD) use hota hai, jo training set matrix X ko U Σ V⑪ mein decompose karta hai — V mein saare PCs ke unit vectors hote hain, sahi order mein.

PCA mein dhyan dene wali baatein

  • Centering zaroori hai: PCA assume karta hai ki dataset origin ke around centered hai. Scikit-Learn ki PCA classes khud centering kar leti hain, par khud implement karo to pehle data ko center karna mat bhoolna.
  • Direction guarantee nahi: PC ke unit vector ki direction guarantee nahi hoti — training set mein chhota sa change bhi direction ulta kar sakta hai, ya do vectors rotate/swap ho sakte hain. Isliye PCA update karo to model ko poora dobara train karo.

Scikit-Learn mein PCA

PCA(n_components=2) aur fit_transform(X) se data 2 dimensions mein aa jata hai. components_ attribute mein pehle d PCs hote hain, aur explained_variance_ratio_ batata hai ki har PC ke along dataset ki variance ka kitna proportion hai. Example mein pehla PC 82% aur doosra 11% variance cover karta hai — teesra PC sirf 7% bachta hai, matlab usmein zyada information nahi hai.

Kitne dimensions rakhein?

Dimensions ki sankhya arbitrarily choose karne ki jagah, itni dimensions rakho jo kaafi variance cover karein — jaise 95%. MNIST (784 features) par 95% variance ke liye sirf 154 dimensions chahiye hote hain! PCA(n_components=0.95) se ye automatically ho jata hai, aur actual components n_components_ mein milte hain. Explained variance ka curve plot karke elbow bhi dekha ja sakta hai — MNIST par lagbhag 100 dimensions tak variance zyada kam nahi hoti. Supervised task ke liye dimensions ki sankhya ko hyperparameter ki tarah tune bhi kar sakte ho — random forest ke saath search mein best combination 57 components aur 475 trees nikla!

PCA for compression

PCA se training set bahut chhota ho jata hai: MNIST 784 se 154 features par aa jata hai — original size ka 20% se bhi kam, sirf 5% variance kho kar! inverse_transform() se reduced data ko wapas 784 dimensions mein decompress bhi kiya ja sakta hai — original data wapas nahi milta, par kareeb hota hai. Original aur reconstructed data ke beech mean squared distance ko reconstruction error kehte hain. Digits thodi quality loss ke saath bhi mostly intact rehte hain.

Randomized aur Incremental PCA

  • Randomized PCA: svd_solver="randomized" pehle d PCs ka fast approximation dhoondhta hai — jab d, n se bahut chhota ho to full SVD se dramatically faster hota hai.
  • Incremental PCA: IncrementalPCA se bade training sets ko mini-batches mein split karke partial_fit() se feed kiya ja sakta hai — poora data memory mein fit hone ki zaroorat nahi. np.memmap se disk par stored bade arrays ko bhi aise hi handle kiya ja sakta hai.
Yaad rakho: Dimensions kam karo to model chhota aur tez hota hai, par zyada kam kar do to signal kho jayega aur model underfit karega. Speed, size aur performance ka sahi balance chuno — aur visualization ke liye hamesha 2 ya 3 dimensions rakho.

# extra code

import numpy as np
from scipy.spatial.transform import Rotation

m = 60
X = np.zeros((m, 3))  # initialize 3D dataset
rng = np.random.default_rng(seed=42)
angles = (rng.random(m) ** 3 + 0.5) * 2 * np.pi  # uneven distribution
X[:, 0], X[:, 1] = np.cos(angles), np.sin(angles) * 0.5  # oval
X += 0.28 * rng.standard_normal((m, 3))  # add more noise
X = Rotation.from_rotvec([np.pi / 29, -np.pi / 20, np.pi / 4]).apply(X)
X += [0.2, 0, 0.2]  # shift a bit

# extra code – this cell generates Figure 7–2

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from sklearn.decomposition import PCA

pca = PCA(n_components=2)
X2D = pca.fit_transform(X)  # dataset reduced to 2D
X3D_inv = pca.inverse_transform(X2D)  # 3D position of the projected samples
X_centered = X - X.mean(axis=0)
U, s, Vt = np.linalg.svd(X_centered)

axes = [-1.4, 1.4, -1.4, 1.4, -1.1, 1.1]
x1, x2 = np.meshgrid(np.linspace(axes[0], axes[1], 10),
                     np.linspace(axes[2], axes[3], 10))
w1, w2 = np.linalg.solve(Vt[:2, :2], Vt[:2, 2])  # projection plane coefs
z = w1 * (x1 - pca.mean_[0]) + w2 * (x2 - pca.mean_[1]) - pca.mean_[2]  # plane
X3D_above = X[X[:, 2] >= X3D_inv[:, 2]]  # samples above plane
X3D_below = X[X[:, 2] < X3D_inv[:, 2]]  # samples below plane

fig = plt.figure(figsize=(9, 9))
ax = fig.add_subplot(111, projection="3d")

# plot samples and projection lines below plane first
ax.plot(X3D_below[:, 0], X3D_below[:, 1], X3D_below[:, 2], "ro", alpha=0.3)
for i in range(m):
    if X[i, 2] < X3D_inv[i, 2]:
        ax.plot([X[i][0], X3D_inv[i][0]],
                [X[i][1], X3D_inv[i][1]],
                [X[i][2], X3D_inv[i][2]], ":", color="#F88")

ax.plot_surface(x1, x2, z, alpha=0.1, color="b")  # projection plane
ax.plot(X3D_inv[:, 0], X3D_inv[:, 1], X3D_inv[:, 2], "b+")  # projected samples
ax.plot(X3D_inv[:, 0], X3D_inv[:, 1], X3D_inv[:, 2], "b.")

# now plot projection lines and samples above plane
for i in range(m):
    if X[i, 2] >= X3D_inv[i, 2]:
        ax.plot([X[i][0], X3D_inv[i][0]],
                [X[i][1], X3D_inv[i][1]],
                [X[i][2], X3D_inv[i][2]], "r--")

ax.plot(X3D_above[:, 0], X3D_above[:, 1], X3D_above[:, 2], "ro")

def set_xyz_axes(ax, axes):
    ax.xaxis.set_rotate_label(False)
    ax.yaxis.set_rotate_label(False)
    ax.zaxis.set_rotate_label(False)
    ax.set_xlabel("$x_1$", labelpad=8, rotation=0)
    ax.set_ylabel("$x_2$", labelpad=8, rotation=0)
    ax.set_zlabel("$x_3$", labelpad=8, rotation=0)
    ax.set_xlim(axes[0:2])
    ax.set_ylim(axes[2:4])
    ax.set_zlim(axes[4:6])

set_xyz_axes(ax, axes)
ax.set_zticks([-1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1])


plt.show()

angle = np.pi / 5
stretch = 5
m = 200

rng = np.random.default_rng(seed=3)
X_line = rng.standard_normal((m, 2)) / 10

X_line = X_line @ [[np.cos(angle), np.sin(angle)],
                   [np.sin(angle), np.cos(angle)]]  # rotate

u1 = np.array([np.cos(angle), np.sin(angle)])
u2 = np.array([np.cos(angle - 2 * np.pi / 6), np.sin(angle - 2 * np.pi / 6)])
u3 = np.array([np.cos(angle - np.pi / 2), np.sin(angle - np.pi / 2)])

# extra code – shows how to construct Σ from s

Σ[:n, :n] = np.diag(s)
assert np.allclose(X_centered, U @ Σ @ Vt)

from sklearn.datasets import fetch_openml

mnist = fetch_openml('mnist_784', as_frame=False)
X_train, y_train = mnist.data[:60_000], mnist.target[:60_000]
X_test, y_test = mnist.data[60_000:], mnist.target[60_000:]

pca = PCA()
pca.fit(X_train)

d = np.argmax(cumsum >= 0.95) + 1  # d equals 154

d

inc_pca.fit(X_mmap)

07.2Chapter 7 · Dimensionality Reduction

Kernel PCA

Is section mein hum Kernel PCA ko dekhte hain — PCA ka wo variant jo nonlinear data ko handle kar sakta hai. Book ke is chapter mein Kernel PCA ka naam technique list mein aata hai, aur iska core idea ye hai ki linear projection jab kaam na kare, to data ko pehle ek higher-dimensional space mein map karke wahan linear PCA lagaya jaye.

Linear PCA ki limit kya hai?

PCA ek linear technique hai: ye data ko ek flat hyperplane par project karta hai. Agar data nonlinear structure rakhta ho — jaise Swiss roll jaisa twisted manifold — to flat projection se layers squash ho jati hain aur structure kho jata hai. Aise data ke liye linear PCA sahi low-dimensional representation nahi bana sakta.

Kernel trick ka idea

Kernel PCA ka idea ye hai: data ko ek nonlinear mapping se ek higher-dimensional feature space mein le jao, jahan structure linear ho jaye, aur wahan PCA apply karo. Kernel trick ki wajah se is higher-dimensional space ko explicitly compute karne ki zaroorat nahi hoti — sirf kernel function se dot products compute kiye jate hain. Isi liye ye nonlinear datasets par bhi kaam kar jata hai, jahan normal PCA fail hota hai.

Kab use karein?

  • Nonlinear data: jab data kisi curved ya twisted manifold par ho aur linear projection structure kharab kar de.
  • Kernel choice: kernel aur uske hyperparameters ka चुनाव result par bahut asar dalta hai, isliye inko cross-validation se tune karna padta hai.
  • Cost: kernel matrix poore dataset par banti hai, isliye bade datasets par ye slow aur memory-heavy ho sakta hai — wahan randomized PCA ya random projection behtar ho sakte hain.
Yaad rakho: Kernel PCA tab yaad rakho jab linear PCA kaam na kare aur data nonlinear ho. Book mein iska detail is Early Release draft mein limited hai — isliye is section mein sirf core idea cover kiya gaya hai, bina koi extra detail invent kiye.
Poora code dekho — Kernel PCA (Notebook 07, Ch 7)
python — Kernel PCA — GitHub: https://github.com/ageron/handson-mlp/blob/main/07_dimensionality_reduction.ipynb
from sklearn.decomposition import KernelPCA

rbf_pca = KernelPCA(n_components=2, kernel="rbf", gamma=0.04, random_state=42)
X_reduced = rbf_pca.fit_transform(X_swiss)

lin_pca = KernelPCA(kernel="linear")
rbf_pca = KernelPCA(kernel="rbf", gamma=0.002)
sig_pca = KernelPCA(kernel="sigmoid", gamma=0.002, coef0=1)

kernel_pcas = ((lin_pca, "Linear kernel"),
               (rbf_pca, rf"RBF kernel, $\gamma={rbf_pca.gamma}$"),
               (sig_pca, rf"Sigmoid kernel, $\gamma={sig_pca.gamma}, r={sig_pca.coef0}$"))

plt.figure(figsize=(11, 3.5))
for idx, (kpca, title) in enumerate(kernel_pcas):
    kpca.n_components = 2
    kpca.random_state = 42
    X_reduced = kpca.fit_transform(X_swiss)

    plt.subplot(1, 3, idx + 1)
    plt.title(title)
    plt.scatter(X_reduced[:, 0], X_reduced[:, 1], c=t, cmap=darker_hot)
    plt.xlabel("$z_1$")
    if idx == 0:
        plt.ylabel("$z_2$", rotation=0)
    plt.grid()

plt.show()

07.3Chapter 7 · Dimensionality Reduction

LDA aur Random Projections

LDA aur random projections — dono dimensionality kam karte hain, par bilkul alag tareeke se. LDA classes ko alag rakhne par focus karta hai, jabki random projection sirf distances ko preserve karne par — bina data ko dekhe bhi!

Random projection kya hai?

Random projection data ko ek random linear projection se lower-dimensional space mein le jata hai. Sunne mein ajeeb lagta hai, par mathematically ye prove hua hai ki aisi random projection distances ko kaafi achhe se preserve karti hai — similar instances similar rehte hain, aur bahut alag instances alag rehte hain. Jitne zyada dimensions drop karoge, utni zyada distances distort hongi.

Kitne dimensions chahiye?

Ek equation batati hai ki distances ko ek tolerance ke andar rakhne ke liye minimum kitne dimensions chahiye: ye sirf instances ki sankhya m aur tolerance ε par depend karti hai, features n par nahi. Example: m = 5,000 instances, n = 20,000 features, aur ε = 10% ho, to d ≥ 7,300 dimensions chahiye. Ye equation Scikit-Learn ke min-dim helper function mein implemented hai.

Scikit-Learn mein random projection

  • GaussianRandomProjection: random matrix banata hai jismein har item Gaussian distribution se sample hota hai (mean 0, variance 1/d). fit() mein dimensionality decide hoti hai, transform() mein projection hota hai. eps aur n_components se control karo.
  • SparseRandomProjection: random matrix sparse hoti hai — sirf lagbhag 1 in 141 cells nonzero hote hain. Isse memory bahut kam lagti hai (lagbhag 25 MB vs 1.2 GB!) aur ye lagbhag 50% faster bhi hai. Sparse input sparse hi rehta hai. Usually yehi prefer karna chahiye, khaas taur par large ya sparse datasets par.

Inverse transform ke liye components matrix ka pseudo-inverse compute karke multiply karna padta hai — par bade matrices par ye bahut slow ho sakta hai.

Random projection kab best hai?

Training almost instantaneous hoti hai, kyunki random matrix banane ke liye sirf dataset ki shape chahiye hoti hai — data khud use hi nahi hota. Ye bahut high-dimensional data (jaise text ya genomics, lakhs features) ya bahut sparse data ke liye perfect hai, jahan randomized PCA bhi slow ho jaye. Trade-off ye hai ki ye PCA se thoda zyada signal khota hai — speed vs performance ka balance hai.

LDA (Linear Discriminant Analysis) kya hai?

LDA ek linear classification algorithm hai jo training ke dauran classes ke beech sabse discriminative axes seekhta hai. In axes ko hyperplane define karne ke liye use karke data ko project kiya ja sakta hai — aur is projection mein classes ek dusre se jitna ho sake door rehti hain. Isliye LDA dimensionality reduce karne ka achha tareeka hai, khaas taur par kisi aur classification algorithm ko chalane se pehle — jab tak LDA akele kaafi na ho. Scikit-Learn mein ye sklearn.discriminant_analysis.LinearDiscriminantAnalysis mein milta hai.

Yaad rakho: Random projection tab chuno jab data bahut high-dimensional ho aur training speed sabse zyada matter kare. LDA tab chuno jab tumhe classes ko alag rakhte hue dimensions kam karne hon — ye supervised technique hai, PCA ki tarah unsupervised nahi.
Poora code dekho — Random projection (Notebook 07, Ch 7)
python — Random projection — GitHub: https://github.com/ageron/handson-mlp/blob/main/07_dimensionality_reduction.ipynb
from sklearn.random_projection import johnson_lindenstrauss_min_dim

m, ε = 5_000, 0.1
d = johnson_lindenstrauss_min_dim(m, eps=ε)
d

# extra code – show the equation computed by johnson_lindenstrauss_min_dim
d = int(4 * np.log(m) / (ε ** 2 / 2 - ε ** 3 / 3))
d

n = 20_000
rng = np.random.default_rng(seed=42)
P = rng.standard_normal((d, n)) / np.sqrt(d)  # std dev = square root of variance

X = rng.standard_normal((m, n))  # generate a fake dataset
X_reduced = X @ P.T

from sklearn.random_projection import GaussianRandomProjection

gaussian_rnd_proj = GaussianRandomProjection(eps=ε, random_state=42)
X_reduced = gaussian_rnd_proj.fit_transform(X)  # same result as above

components_pinv = np.linalg.pinv(gaussian_rnd_proj.components_)
X_recovered = X_reduced @ components_pinv.T

# extra code – performance comparison between Gaussian and Sparse RP

from sklearn.random_projection import SparseRandomProjection

print("GaussianRandomProjection fit")
%timeit GaussianRandomProjection(random_state=42).fit(X)
print("SparseRandomProjection fit")
%timeit SparseRandomProjection(random_state=42).fit(X)

gaussian_rnd_proj = GaussianRandomProjection(random_state=42).fit(X)
sparse_rnd_proj = SparseRandomProjection(random_state=42).fit(X)
print("GaussianRandomProjection transform")
%timeit gaussian_rnd_proj.transform(X)
print("SparseRandomProjection transform")
%timeit sparse_rnd_proj.transform(X)

07.4Chapter 7 · Dimensionality Reduction

LLE aur Other Techniques — Manifold Learning

LLE, MDS, Isomap aur t-SNE — ye sab manifold learning techniques hain. Ye data ki twisted, nonlinear structure ko samajh kar use unroll ya preserve karte hain, jahan projection-based methods fail ho jate hain.

LLE (Locally Linear Embedding) kaise kaam karta hai?

LLE ek nonlinear dimensionality reduction technique hai jo projection par depend nahi karti. Iske do steps hote hain: pehle, har training instance ke k-nearest neighbors dhoondho aur us instance ko un neighbors ke linear combination ke roop mein reconstruct karne wale weights seekho. Doosre, unhi weights ko fixed rakhkar instances ko low-dimensional space mein aise place karo ki local relationships best preserve hon. Swiss roll par LLE kamaal karta hai — poora roll unroll ho jata hai aur local distances preserve rehti hain, halanki large-scale distances preserve nahi hoti (unrolled shape rectangle ki jagah stretched band jaisa dikhta hai).

  • Code: LocallyLinearEmbedding(n_components=2, n_neighbors=10) se Swiss roll ko 2D mein unroll kiya jata hai.
  • Strength: twisted manifolds ko unroll karne mein bahut achha, khaas taur par jab noise zyada na ho.
  • Weakness: scale achhe se nahi karta — complexity mein m² term ki wajah se bade datasets par slow ho jata hai. Mostly small ya medium datasets ke liye hai.

MDS (Multidimensional Scaling)

MDS dimensionality kam karte hue instances ke beech ki distances ko preserve karne ki koshish karta hai. Swiss roll par MDS roll ko flatten kar deta hai bina uski global curvature khoye.

Isomap

Isomap har instance ko uske nearest neighbors se connect karke ek graph banata hai, phir geodesic distances (graph mein shortest path par nodes ki sankhya) ko preserve karte hue dimensionality kam karta hai. Ye tab best kaam karta hai jab data ek smooth, low-dimensional manifold par ho jiska ek single global structure ho — jaise Swiss roll, jahan Isomap curvature ko poori tarah drop kar deta hai.

t-SNE

t-SNE similar instances ko paas aur dissimilar instances ko door rakhne ki koshish karta hai. Ye mostly visualization ke liye use hota hai — khaas taur par high-dimensional space mein clusters ko visualize karne ke liye, jaise MNIST images ka 2D map. Ye ML model ke liye preprocessing stage ke roop mein use karne ke liye nahi bana hai. Swiss roll par t-SNE roll ko flatten karta hai, thodi curvature preserve karta hai, aur clusters ko amplify karke roll ko tod bhi deta hai.

UMAP

UMAP ek aur popular visualization technique hai. t-SNE local structure (khaas taur par clusters) ko preserve karne mein behtar hai, jabki UMAP local aur global dono structures ko preserve karne ki koshish karta hai, aur bade datasets par behtar scale karta hai. Ye Scikit-Learn mein available nahi hai — iske liye umap-learn package use hota hai.

Yaad rakho: Large-scale structure preserve karna achha hai ya bura — ye downstream task par depend karta hai. Har technique ka apna trade-off hai; visualization ke liye t-SNE ya UMAP, aur smooth manifold ke liye Isomap ya LLE try karo.

from sklearn.preprocessing import MinMaxScaler
from matplotlib.offsetbox import AnnotationBbox, OffsetImage

def plot_digits(X, y, min_distance=0.04, images=None, figsize=(13, 10)):
    # Let's scale the input features so that they range from 0 to 1
    X_normalized = MinMaxScaler().fit_transform(X)
    # Now we create the list of coordinates of the digits plotted so far.
    # We pretend that one is already plotted far away at the start, to
    # avoid `if` statements in the loop below
    neighbors = np.array([[10., 10.]])
    # The rest should be self-explanatory
    plt.figure(figsize=figsize)
    cmap = plt.cm.jet
    digits = np.unique(y)
    for digit in digits:
        plt.scatter(X_normalized[y == digit, 0], X_normalized[y == digit, 1],
                    c=[cmap(float(digit) / 9)], alpha=0.5)
    plt.axis("off")
    ax = plt.gca()  # get current axes
    for index, image_coord in enumerate(X_normalized):
        closest_distance = np.linalg.norm(neighbors - image_coord, axis=1).min()
        if closest_distance > min_distance:
            neighbors = np.r_[neighbors, [image_coord]]
            if images is None:
                plt.text(image_coord[0], image_coord[1], str(int(y[index])),
                         color=cmap(float(y[index]) / 9),
                         fontdict={"weight": "bold", "size": 16})
            else:
                image = images[index].reshape(28, 28)
                imagebox = AnnotationBbox(OffsetImage(image, cmap="binary"),
                                          image_coord)
                ax.add_artist(imagebox)

plot_digits(X_reduced, y_sample)

plot_digits(X_reduced, y_sample, images=X_sample, figsize=(35, 25))

plot_digits(X_subset_reduced, y_subset, images=X_subset, figsize=(22, 22))

%time X_pca_reduced = pca.fit_transform(X_sample)

)

%time X_lda_reduced = lda.fit_transform(X_sample, y_sample)

08Chapter 8 · Unsupervised Learning Techniques

Unsupervised Learning Techniques

Aaj ke zyada tar ML applications supervised learning par based hain, par available data ka bahut bada hissa unlabeled hai — input features X hain, par labels y nahi hain. Unsupervised learning mein bahut bada potential hai jo abhi sirf shuru hua hai.

Unsupervised learning kyun zaroori hai?

Socho ek manufacturing line par defective items detect karne hain. Pictures lena aasan hai — roz hazaaron pictures mil jayengi. Par har picture ko manually label karna (defective ya normal) bahut lamba, costly aur tedious kaam hai, jo sirf chhote subset par hi ho pata hai. Result: labeled dataset chhota, classifier ki performance disappointing. Unsupervised learning yahi problem solve karta hai — bina labels ke data se seekhna.

Is chapter ke teen main tasks

  • Clustering: similar instances ko groups (clusters) mein baantna. Customer segmentation, recommender systems, search engines, image segmentation, semi-supervised learning aur dimensionality reduction mein use hota hai.
  • Anomaly detection (outlier detection): ye seekhna ki normal data kaisa dikhta hai, aur phir abnormal instances ko detect karna. Fraud detection, defective products, time series mein naye trends, ya model train karne se pehle outliers hatane mein useful hai.
  • Density estimation: us random process ki probability density function (PDF) estimate karna jisne dataset generate kiya. Anomaly detection mein use hota hai — bahut low-density regions mein located instances likely anomalies hote hain.

Chapter 7 mein hum dimensionality reduction dekh chuke hain — jo sabse common unsupervised task hai. Is chapter mein hum clustering algorithms (k-means aur DBSCAN), Gaussian mixture models, aur anomaly/novelty detection ko dekhenge.

Yaad rakho: Clustering mein koi universal definition nahi hoti ki cluster kya hai — ye context par depend karta hai, aur alag algorithms alag tarah ke clusters capture karte hain. Koi ek algorithm har jagah best nahi hota.

08.1Chapter 8 · Unsupervised Learning Techniques

Clustering — K-Means

K-means ek simple aur fast clustering algorithm hai jo blobs jaise datasets ko kuch hi iterations mein cluster kar deta hai. Iska idea bahut simple hai: centroids dhoondho, har instance ko sabse kareeb centroid wale cluster mein daalo, phir centroids ko update karo — aur ye repeat karo jab tak centroids ruk na jayein.

K-means kaise kaam karta hai?

  • Step 1: centroids ko randomly place karo (jaise k instances ko randomly pick karke).
  • Step 2: har instance ko sabse kareeb centroid wale cluster mein assign karo (label karo).
  • Step 3: har cluster ka centroid update karo — us cluster ke instances ka mean lo.
  • Step 4: repeat karo jab tak centroids move karna band na kar dein.

Algorithm converge karna guaranteed hai, kyunki instances aur unke closest centroids ke beech mean squared distance har step par sirf kam ho sakti hai. Par ye sahi solution par converge kare, ye guarantee nahi hai — ye centroid initialization par depend karta hai, aur local optimum mein phas sakta hai.

Scikit-Learn mein k-means

KMeans(n_clusters=5, random_state=42) se 5 clusters banaye jate hain. labels_ mein har instance ka cluster index hota hai, cluster_centers_ mein centroids, aur predict() se naye instances ko sabse kareeb centroid wale cluster mein assign kiya jata hai. Decision boundaries Voronoi tessellation jaisi dikhti hain. transform() har instance ki har centroid se distance deta hai — ye soft clustering hai, aur high-dimensional data ko k-dimensional mein badal kar nonlinear dimensionality reduction bhi kar sakta hai.

Centroid initialization — k-means++

Random initialization se suboptimal solutions mil sakte hain. Iske solutions: centroids ko manually dena (init mein array), ya algorithm ko kai baar alag random initializations ke saath chalakar best solution rakhna — n_init se control hota hai. Best solution inertia se chuna jata hai — inertia har instance aur uske closest centroid ke beech squared distances ka sum hoti hai. Smarter initialization k-means++ hai (default init="k-means++"): pehla centroid randomly, phir har naya centroid un instances mein se choose hota hai jo pehle se chune centroids se door hain. Isse optimal solution milne ki probability bahut badh jati hai.

Mini-batch k-means

Bade datasets ke liye MiniBatchKMeans use hota hai — har iteration mein poora dataset use karne ki jagah mini-batches use karta hai aur centroids ko thoda-thoda move karta hai. Isse huge datasets bhi cluster kiye ja sakte hain jo memory mein fit na hon.

Optimal k kaise chunein?

  • Elbow method: inertia ko k ke function ke roop mein plot karo — jahan curve ka elbow ho (jaise k = 4), wo achha choice ho sakta hai. Par inertia hamesha k badhne par kam hoti hai, isliye ye metric akele kaafi nahi hai.
  • Silhouette score: har instance ka silhouette coefficient (b − a) / max(a, b) hota hai, jahan a same cluster ke instances se mean distance hai aur b next closest cluster se mean distance. Score −1 se +1 ke beech hota hai; +1 ke kareeb matlab instance apne cluster mein achhe se fit hai. Silhouette diagram mein har cluster ek knife shape hota hai — width jitni zyada, utna behtar.

K-means ki limits

K-means ko kai baar chalana padta hai, clusters ki sankhya pehle se specify karni padti hai, aur ye varying sizes, densities ya nonspherical shapes wale clusters par achha nahi karta — jaise ellipsoidal clusters ko ye galat tareeke se kaat deta hai. Isliye features ko pehle scale karna bahut zaroori hai, warna clusters stretch ho jayenge aur k-means kharab perform karega.

Yaad rakho: K-means generally fastest clustering algorithms mein se ek hai, par ye assume karta hai ki saare clusters lagbhag same size, density aur round shape ke hain. Ellipsoidal clusters ke liye Gaussian mixture models behtar hote hain.

from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
from sklearn.datasets import make_blobs

                  random_state=7)

def plot_clusters(X, y=None):
    plt.scatter(X[:, 0], X[:, 1], c=y, s=1)
    plt.xlabel("$x_1$")
    plt.ylabel("$x_2$", rotation=0)

plt.figure(figsize=(8, 4))

y_pred is kmeans.labels_

import numpy as np

X_new = np.array([[0, 2], [3, 2], [-3, 3], [-3, 2.5]])
kmeans.predict(X_new)

# extra code – this cell generates Figure 8–3

def plot_data(X):
    plt.plot(X[:, 0], X[:, 1], 'k.', markersize=2)

def plot_centroids(centroids, weights=None, circle_color='w', cross_color='k'):
    if weights is not None:
        centroids = centroids[weights > weights.max() / 10]
    plt.scatter(centroids[:, 0], centroids[:, 1],
                marker='o', s=35, linewidths=8,
                color=circle_color, zorder=10, alpha=0.9)
    plt.scatter(centroids[:, 0], centroids[:, 1],
                marker='x', s=2, linewidths=12,
                color=cross_color, zorder=11, alpha=1)

def plot_decision_boundaries(clusterer, X, resolution=1000, show_centroids=True,
                             show_xlabels=True, show_ylabels=True):
    mins = X.min(axis=0) - 0.1
    maxs = X.max(axis=0) + 0.1
    xx, yy = np.meshgrid(np.linspace(mins[0], maxs[0], resolution),
                         np.linspace(mins[1], maxs[1], resolution))
    Z = clusterer.predict(np.c_[xx.ravel(), yy.ravel()])
    Z = Z.reshape(xx.shape)

    plt.contourf(Z, extent=(mins[0], maxs[0], mins[1], maxs[1]),
                cmap="Pastel2")
    plt.contour(Z, extent=(mins[0], maxs[0], mins[1], maxs[1]),
                linewidths=1, colors='k')
    plot_data(X)
    if show_centroids:
        plot_centroids(clusterer.cluster_centers_)

    if show_xlabels:
        plt.xlabel("$x_1$")
    else:
        plt.tick_params(labelbottom=False)
    if show_ylabels:
        plt.ylabel("$x_2$", rotation=0)
    else:
        plt.tick_params(labelleft=False)

plt.figure(figsize=(8, 4))
plot_decision_boundaries(kmeans, X)

plt.show()

kmeans.transform(X_new).round(2)

# extra code
np.linalg.norm(np.tile(X_new, (1, k)).reshape(-1, k, 2)
               - kmeans.cluster_centers_, axis=2).round(2)

# extra code – this cell generates Figure 8–9

from sklearn.metrics import silhouette_samples
from matplotlib.ticker import FixedLocator, FixedFormatter

plt.figure(figsize=(11, 9))

for k in (3, 4, 5, 6):
    plt.subplot(2, 2, k - 2)

    y_pred = kmeans_per_k[k - 1].labels_
    silhouette_coefficients = silhouette_samples(X, y_pred)

    padding = len(X) // 30
    pos = padding
    ticks = []
    for i in range(k):
        coeffs = silhouette_coefficients[y_pred == i]
        coeffs.sort()

        color = plt.cm.Spectral(i / k)
        plt.fill_betweenx(np.arange(pos, pos + len(coeffs)), 0, coeffs,
                          facecolor=color, edgecolor=color, alpha=0.7)
        ticks.append(pos + len(coeffs) // 2)
        pos += len(coeffs) + padding

    plt.gca().yaxis.set_major_locator(FixedLocator(ticks))
    plt.gca().yaxis.set_major_formatter(FixedFormatter(range(k)))
    if k in (3, 5):
        plt.ylabel("Cluster")

    if k in (5, 6):
        plt.gca().set_xticks([-0.1, 0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, 1])
        plt.xlabel("Silhouette Coefficient")
    else:
        plt.tick_params(labelbottom=False)

    plt.axvline(x=silhouette_scores[k - 2], color="red", linestyle="--")
    plt.title(f"$k={k}$")


plt.show()

from pathlib import Path

homlp_root = "https://github.com/ageron/handson-mlp/raw/main/"

import PIL

image = np.asarray(PIL.Image.open(filepath))
image.shape

kmeans = KMeans(n_clusters=8, random_state=42).fit(X)

segmented_img = segmented_img.reshape(image.shape)

# extra code – this cell generates Figure 8–11

segmented_imgs = []
n_colors = (10, 8, 6, 4, 2)
for n_clusters in n_colors:
    kmeans = KMeans(n_clusters=n_clusters, random_state=42).fit(X)
    segmented_img = kmeans.cluster_centers_[kmeans.labels_]
    segmented_imgs.append(segmented_img.reshape(image.shape))

plt.figure(figsize=(10, 5))
plt.subplots_adjust(wspace=0.05, hspace=0.1)

plt.subplot(2, 3, 1)
plt.imshow(image)

plt.axis('off')

for idx, n_clusters in enumerate(n_colors):
    plt.subplot(2, 3, 2 + idx)
    plt.imshow(segmented_imgs[idx] / 255)
    plt.title(f"{n_clusters} colors")
    plt.axis('off')

from sklearn.datasets import load_digits

X_digits, y_digits = load_digits(return_X_y=True)
X_train, y_train = X_digits[:1400], y_digits[:1400]
X_test, y_test = X_digits[1400:], y_digits[1400:]

from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression

n_labeled = 50
log_reg = LogisticRegression(max_iter=10_000)
log_reg.fit(X_train[:n_labeled], y_train[:n_labeled])

log_reg.score(X_test, y_test)

# extra code – measure the accuracy when we use the whole training set
log_reg_full = LogisticRegression(max_iter=10_000)
log_reg_full.fit(X_train, y_train)
log_reg_full.score(X_test, y_test)

k = 50
kmeans = KMeans(n_clusters=k, random_state=42)
X_digits_dist = kmeans.fit_transform(X_train)
representative_digit_idx = X_digits_dist.argmin(axis=0)
X_representative_digits = X_train[representative_digit_idx]

# extra code – this cell generates Figure 8–12

plt.figure(figsize=(8, 2))
for index, X_representative_digit in enumerate(X_representative_digits):
    plt.subplot(k // 10, 10, index + 1)
    plt.imshow(X_representative_digit.reshape(8, 8), cmap="binary",
               interpolation="bilinear")
    plt.axis('off')


plt.show()

y_representative_digits = np.array([
    8, 0, 1, 3, 6, 7, 5, 4, 2, 8,
    2, 3, 9, 5, 3, 9, 1, 7, 9, 1,
    4, 6, 9, 7, 5, 2, 2, 1, 3, 3,
    6, 0, 4, 9, 8, 1, 8, 4, 2, 4,
    2, 3, 9, 7, 8, 9, 6, 5, 6, 4,
])

log_reg = LogisticRegression(max_iter=10_000)
log_reg.fit(X_representative_digits, y_representative_digits)
log_reg.score(X_test, y_test)

y_train_propagated = np.empty(len(X_train), dtype=np.int64)
for i in range(k):
    y_train_propagated[kmeans.labels_ == i] = y_representative_digits[i]

log_reg = LogisticRegression(max_iter=10_000)
log_reg.fit(X_train, y_train_propagated)

log_reg.score(X_test, y_test)

percentile_closest = 50

X_cluster_dist = X_digits_dist[np.arange(len(X_train)), kmeans.labels_]
for i in range(k):
    in_cluster = (kmeans.labels_ == i)
    cluster_dist = X_cluster_dist[in_cluster]
    cutoff_distance = np.percentile(cluster_dist, percentile_closest)
    above_cutoff = (X_cluster_dist > cutoff_distance)
    X_cluster_dist[in_cluster & above_cutoff] = -1

partially_propagated = (X_cluster_dist != -1)
X_train_partially_propagated = X_train[partially_propagated]
y_train_partially_propagated = y_train_propagated[partially_propagated]

log_reg = LogisticRegression(max_iter=10_000)
log_reg.fit(X_train_partially_propagated, y_train_partially_propagated)
log_reg.score(X_test, y_test)

(y_train_partially_propagated == y_train[partially_propagated]).mean()

08.2Chapter 8 · Unsupervised Learning Techniques

Hierarchical Clustering aur DBSCAN

K-means har shape ke clusters nahi dhoondh sakta. DBSCAN density-based approach use karta hai — continuous high-density regions ko cluster manta hai — aur isse kisi bhi shape ke clusters mil sakte hain, saath mein outliers bhi detect hote hain. Hierarchical clustering ek aur approach hai jo clusters ka tree banata hai.

DBSCAN kaise kaam karta hai?

  • ε-neighborhood: har instance ke liye dekho ki uske ε distance ke andar kitne instances hain.
  • Core instance: agar kisi instance ke neighborhood mein kam se kam min_samples instances hain (khud ko bhi count karke), to wo core instance hai — dense region mein hai.
  • Cluster: core instance ke neighborhood ke saare instances usi cluster mein aate hain; neighboring core instances ki chain se ek hi bada cluster banta hai.
  • Anomaly: jo instance core nahi hai aur uske neighborhood mein koi core instance bhi nahi hai, wo anomaly mana jata hai.

Moons dataset par DBSCAN(eps=0.05, min_samples=5) se 7 clusters aur bahut saari anomalies mili — disappointing! Par eps=0.2 karne se perfect clustering mili. Labels mein −1 ka matlab hai anomaly. Core instances core_sample_indices_ aur components_ mein milte hain.

DBSCAN se prediction kaise karein?

DBSCAN class mein predict() method nahi hoti — sirf fit_predict(). Naye instances ke liye khud classifier train karna padta hai, jaise core instances par KNeighborsClassifier. Maximum distance ka rule lagakar door ke instances ko anomaly bhi declare kiya ja sakta hai. DBSCAN simple aur powerful hai, sirf do hyperparameters (eps aur min_samples) hain, par agar clusters ki density bahut alag ho ya low-density region na ho, to ye struggle karta hai. Iski complexity lagbhag O(m²n) hoti hai, isliye bade datasets par slow ho jata hai. Varying densities ke liye HDBSCAN (sklearn.cluster.HDBSCAN) aksar behtar hota hai.

Agglomerative (hierarchical) clustering

Hierarchical clustering mein clusters ki hierarchy bottom-up banti hai: shuru mein har instance apna cluster hota hai, phir har iteration mein sabse kareeb do clusters merge hote hain, jab tak ek bada cluster na ban jaye. Isse ek binary tree milta hai jiske leaves individual instances hote hain. Ye kisi bhi shape ke clusters capture kar sakta hai, aur kisi ek cluster scale ko force karne ki jagah ek flexible, informative tree deta hai. Connectivity matrix dene se ye bade datasets par bhi scale kar sakta hai.

Doosre clustering algorithms

  • BIRCH: bahut bade datasets ke liye design hua hai; limited memory mein kaam karta hai aur batch k-means se tez ho sakta hai, jab features 20 se kam hon.
  • Mean-shift: har instance par circle rakhkar use density ke mean ki taraf shift karta hai, jab tak circles ruk na jayein. Kisi bhi shape aur sankhya ke clusters dhoondh sakta hai, par internal density variations par clusters ko tod deta hai, aur bade datasets par slow hota hai.
  • Affinity propagation: instances ek dusre ko messages bhejkar exemplars elect karte hain; clusters ki sankhya pehle se specify karne ki zaroorat nahi hoti. Par complexity O(m²) hoti hai.
  • Spectral clustering: similarity matrix se low-dimensional embedding banakar usmein clustering karta hai (Scikit-Learn mein k-means use hota hai). Complex structures capture kar sakta hai aur graphs ko cut kar sakta hai, par bade datasets par scale nahi karta.

Clustering ke applications

Image segmentation: pixels ko unke color ke hisaab se cluster karke har pixel ka color uske cluster ke mean color se replace kar do — colors ki sankhya bahut kam ho jati hai. 8 clusters par ladybug image achhi tarah segment hoti hai; kam clusters par ladybug ka red color apna cluster kho deta hai, kyunki k-means similar sizes wale clusters prefer karta hai. Semi-supervised learning: digits dataset par sirf 50 labeled instances se logistic regression 75.8% accuracy deta hai. 50 clusters ke representative images (centroid ke sabse kareeb) ko label karke 83.1% milti hai. Labels ko poore cluster mein propagate karke 87.2%, aur door ke 50% outliers ko hatakar 88.4% accuracy milti hai — sirf 50 labels se, full labeled data ke 90.9% ke kareeb! Active learning: model jin instances par sabse uncertain ho, unko expert se label karwao, aur repeat karo jab tak improvement worth ho.

Yaad rakho: DBSCAN ko k ki zaroorat nahi hoti — ye clusters ki sankhya khud dhoondhta hai aur outliers ko −1 label deta hai. Par eps ko tune karna bahut zaroori hai: bahut chhota eps bahut saare chhote clusters aur anomalies dega.

# extra code – this cell generates Figure 8–13

def plot_dbscan(dbscan, X, size, show_xlabels=True, show_ylabels=True):
    core_mask = np.zeros_like(dbscan.labels_, dtype=bool)
    core_mask[dbscan.core_sample_indices_] = True
    anomalies_mask = dbscan.labels_ == -1
    non_core_mask = ~(core_mask | anomalies_mask)

    cores = dbscan.components_
    anomalies = X[anomalies_mask]
    non_cores = X[non_core_mask]

    plt.scatter(cores[:, 0], cores[:, 1],
                c=dbscan.labels_[core_mask], marker='o', s=size, cmap="Paired")
    plt.scatter(cores[:, 0], cores[:, 1], marker='*', s=20,
                c=dbscan.labels_[core_mask])
    plt.scatter(anomalies[:, 0], anomalies[:, 1],
                c="r", marker="x", s=100)
    plt.scatter(non_cores[:, 0], non_cores[:, 1],
                c=dbscan.labels_[non_core_mask], marker=".")
    if show_xlabels:
        plt.xlabel("$x_1$")
    else:
        plt.tick_params(labelbottom=False)
    if show_ylabels:
        plt.ylabel("$x_2$", rotation=0)
    else:
        plt.tick_params(labelleft=False)
    plt.title(f"eps={dbscan.eps:.2f}, min_samples={dbscan.min_samples}")
    plt.grid()
    plt.gca().set_axisbelow(True)

dbscan2 = DBSCAN(eps=0.2)
dbscan2.fit(X)

plt.figure(figsize=(9, 3.2))

plt.subplot(121)
plot_dbscan(dbscan, X, size=100)

plt.subplot(122)

08.3Chapter 8 · Unsupervised Learning Techniques

Gaussian Mixtures

Gaussian mixture model (GMM) ek probabilistic model hai jo assume karta hai ki instances kai Gaussian distributions ke mixture se generate hue hain. Har Gaussian ek ellipsoidal cluster banata hai — alag shape, size, density aur orientation ke saath. Ye k-means se zyada flexible hai.

GMM kaise kaam karta hai?

Har instance ke liye pehle ek cluster randomly pick hota hai (us cluster ke weight ke hisaab se), phir us cluster ki Gaussian distribution se instance ki location sample hoti hai. Model ko train karne ka matlab hai weights, means aur covariance matrices ko estimate karna. Scikit-Learn mein GaussianMixture(n_components=3, n_init=10) se ye aasani se hota hai. Example mein true weights 0.4, 0.4 aur 0.2 the, aur algorithm ne lagbhag wahi dhoondhe.

EM algorithm

GMM expectation-maximization (EM) algorithm se train hota hai, jo k-means jaisa hi hai: pehle instances ko clusters mein assign karo (expectation step), phir clusters ko update karo (maximization step) — aur repeat karo jab tak convergence na ho. Farq ye hai ki EM soft assignments use karta hai: har instance ke liye har cluster ki probability estimate hoti hai (responsibilities), aur har cluster ka update saare instances se hota hai, har instance us probability se weighted. K-means ki tarah EM bhi poor solutions par converge kar sakta hai, isliye n_init=10 jaise multiple runs zaroori hain (default n_init=1 hota hai — dhyan rakho!). converged_ aur n_iter_ se check karo ki algorithm converge hua ya nahi.

GMM se kya-kya kar sakte ho?

  • Hard clustering: predict() se har instance ko sabse likely cluster mein daalo.
  • Soft clustering: predict_proba() se har cluster ki probability lo.
  • New samples: GMM ek generative model hai — sample() se naye instances generate kar sakte ho.
  • Density estimation: score_samples() se kisi bhi location par log probability density milti hai — score zyada matlab density zyada.

Covariance types

  • full (default): har cluster koi bhi shape, size aur orientation le sakta hai.
  • spherical: saare clusters spherical hote hain, par diameters alag ho sakte hain.
  • diag: ellipsoidal shape koi bhi, par axes coordinate axes ke parallel hone chahiye.
  • tied: saare clusters ki shape, size aur orientation same hoti hai (ek hi covariance matrix).

Constraints se parameters kam hote hain aur training aasan hoti hai. Spherical ya diag ki complexity O(kmn) hoti hai, jabki tied ya full ki O(kmn² + kn³) — isliye full bade feature sets par scale nahi karta.

Clusters ki sankhya kaise chunein?

K-means wale inertia ya silhouette score yahan reliable nahi hote, kyunki clusters spherical nahi hote. Iske bajay BIC (Bayesian information criterion) ya AIC (Akaike information criterion) use karo — dono zyada parameters wale models ko penalize karte hain aur achhe fit ko reward karte hain. gm.bic(X) aur gm.aic(X) se values milti hain; example mein dono k = 3 par lowest the. BIC usually AIC se simpler model chunta hai.

Bayesian Gaussian mixture

BayesianGaussianMixture clusters ki sankhya khud dhoondh sakta hai: n_components ko optimal se zyada set karo (jaise 10), aur algorithm unnecessary clusters ko zero ke kareeb weight dekar eliminate kar deta hai. Example mein 10 mein se sirf 3 clusters ke weights nonzero rahe — 0.4, 0.21 aur 0.39. Par GMM ellipsoidal shapes par hi achha hai — moons jaise non-ellipsoidal clusters par ye 2 ki jagah 8 clusters dhoondh leta hai.

Yaad rakho: GMM ko k-means ka generalization samjho — ye sirf centers nahi, har cluster ki size, shape, orientation aur weight bhi seekhta hai. Isi flexibility ki wajah se ye ellipsoidal clusters par k-means se bahut behtar hai.

from matplotlib.colors import LogNorm

def plot_gaussian_mixture(clusterer, X, resolution=1000, show_ylabels=True):
    mins = X.min(axis=0) - 0.1
    maxs = X.max(axis=0) + 0.1
    xx, yy = np.meshgrid(np.linspace(mins[0], maxs[0], resolution),
                         np.linspace(mins[1], maxs[1], resolution))
    Z = -clusterer.score_samples(np.c_[xx.ravel(), yy.ravel()])
    Z = Z.reshape(xx.shape)

    plt.contourf(xx, yy, Z,
                 norm=LogNorm(vmin=1.0, vmax=30.0),
                 levels=np.logspace(0, 2, 12))
    plt.contour(xx, yy, Z,
                norm=LogNorm(vmin=1.0, vmax=30.0),
                levels=np.logspace(0, 2, 12),
                linewidths=1, colors='k')

    Z = clusterer.predict(np.c_[xx.ravel(), yy.ravel()])
    Z = Z.reshape(xx.shape)
    plt.contour(xx, yy, Z,
                linewidths=2, colors='r', linestyles='dashed')

    plt.plot(X[:, 0], X[:, 1], 'k.', markersize=2)
    plot_centroids(clusterer.means_, clusterer.weights_)

    plt.xlabel("$x_1$")
    if show_ylabels:
        plt.ylabel("$x_2$", rotation=0)
    else:
        plt.tick_params(labelleft=False)

plt.figure(figsize=(8, 4))

plot_gaussian_mixture(gm, X)


plt.show()

# extra code – this cell generates Figure 8–18

from scipy.stats import norm

x_val = 2.5
std_val = 1.3
x_range = [-6, 4]
x_proba_range = [-2, 2]
stds_range = [1, 2]

xs = np.linspace(x_range[0], x_range[1], 501)
stds = np.linspace(stds_range[0], stds_range[1], 501)
Xs, Stds = np.meshgrid(xs, stds)
Z = 2 * norm.pdf(Xs - 1.0, 0, Stds) + norm.pdf(Xs + 4.0, 0, Stds)
Z = Z / Z.sum(axis=1)[:, np.newaxis] / (xs[1] - xs[0])

x_example_idx = (xs >= x_val).argmax()  # index of the first value >= x_val
max_idx = Z[:, x_example_idx].argmax()
max_val = Z[:, x_example_idx].max()
s_example_idx = (stds >= std_val).argmax()
x_range_min_idx = (xs >= x_proba_range[0]).argmax()
x_range_max_idx = (xs >= x_proba_range[1]).argmax()
log_max_idx = np.log(Z[:, x_example_idx]).argmax()
log_max_val = np.log(Z[:, x_example_idx]).max()

plt.figure(figsize=(8, 4.5))

plt.subplot(2, 2, 1)
plt.contourf(Xs, Stds, Z, cmap="GnBu")
plt.plot([-6, 4], [std_val, std_val], "k-", linewidth=2)
plt.plot([x_val, x_val], [1, 2], "b-", linewidth=2)
plt.ylabel(r"$\theta$", rotation=0, labelpad=10)
plt.title(r"Model $f(x; \theta)$")

plt.subplot(2, 2, 2)
plt.plot(stds, Z[:, x_example_idx], "b-")
plt.plot(stds[max_idx], max_val, "r.")
plt.plot([stds[max_idx], stds[max_idx]], [0, max_val], "r:")
plt.plot([0, stds[max_idx]], [max_val, max_val], "r:")
plt.text(stds[max_idx]+ 0.01, 0.081, r"$\hat{\theta}$")
plt.text(stds[max_idx]+ 0.01, max_val - 0.006, r"$Max$")
plt.text(1.01, max_val - 0.008, r"$\hat{\mathcal{L}}$")
plt.ylabel(r"$\mathcal{L}$", rotation=0, labelpad=10)
plt.title(fr"$\mathcal{{L}}(\theta|x={x_val}) = f(x={x_val}; \theta)$")
plt.grid()
plt.axis([1, 2, 0.08, 0.12])

plt.subplot(2, 2, 3)
plt.plot(xs, Z[s_example_idx], "k-")
plt.fill_between(xs[x_range_min_idx:x_range_max_idx+1],
                 Z[s_example_idx, x_range_min_idx:x_range_max_idx+1], alpha=0.2)
plt.xlabel(r"$x$")
plt.ylabel("PDF")
plt.title(fr"PDF $f(x; \theta={std_val})$")
plt.grid()
plt.axis([-6, 4, 0, 0.25])

plt.subplot(2, 2, 4)
plt.plot(stds, np.log(Z[:, x_example_idx]), "b-")
plt.plot(stds[log_max_idx], log_max_val, "r.")
plt.plot([stds[log_max_idx], stds[log_max_idx]], [-5, log_max_val], "r:")
plt.plot([0, stds[log_max_idx]], [log_max_val, log_max_val], "r:")
plt.text(stds[log_max_idx]+ 0.01, log_max_val - 0.06, r"$Max$")
plt.text(stds[log_max_idx]+ 0.01, -2.49, r"$\hat{\theta}$")
plt.text(1.01, log_max_val - 0.08, r"$\log \, \hat{\mathcal{L}}$")
plt.xlabel(r"$\theta$")
plt.ylabel(r"$\log\mathcal{L}$", rotation=0, labelpad=10)
plt.title(fr"$\log \, \mathcal{{L}}(\theta|x={x_val})$")
plt.grid()

plt.figure(figsize=(8, 3))
plt.plot(range(1, 11), bics, "bo-", label="BIC")
plt.plot(range(1, 11), aics, "go--", label="AIC")
plt.xlabel("$k$")
plt.ylabel("Information Criterion")
plt.axis([1, 9.5, min(aics) - 50, max(aics) + 50])
plt.annotate("", xy=(3, bics[2]), xytext=(3.4, 8650),
             arrowprops=dict(facecolor='black', shrink=0.1))
plt.text(3.5, 8660, "Minimum", horizontalalignment="center")
plt.legend()
plt.grid()

plt.show()

08.4Chapter 8 · Unsupervised Learning Techniques

Anomaly Detection aur Novelty Detection

Anomaly detection ka matlab hai ye seekhna ki normal data kaisa dikhta hai, aur phir abnormal instances ko pakadna. Fraud detection, defective products, naye trends ya dataset ko clean karne mein ye bahut kaam aata hai.

GMM se anomaly detection

GMM se anomaly detection bahut simple hai: jo instance low-density region mein ho, wo anomaly hai. Pehle density threshold define karo. Jaise defective products ka ratio 2% hai, to threshold wahan set karo jahan 2% instances usse neeche density mein hon. score_samples() se densities nikalo, np.percentile(densities, 2) se threshold lo, aur usse neeche wale instances anomalies hain. Zyada false positives hon to threshold kam karo, zyada false negatives hon to threshold badhao — yehi precision/recall trade-off hai. Dhyan rakho: GMM saare data ko fit karta hai, outliers ko bhi — isse normal ka view bias ho sakta hai. Solution: ek baar fit karke extreme outliers hatakar dobara fit karo, ya robust covariance estimation use karo.

Anomaly detection vs novelty detection

Novelty detection mein algorithm ko clean dataset par train kiya jata hai, jismein outliers nahi hote — jabki anomaly detection mein aisa assumption nahi hota. Outlier detection aksar dataset ko clean karne ke liye use hota hai.

Doosre anomaly detection algorithms

  • Fast-MCD / EllipticEnvelope: assume karta hai ki normal instances ek hi Gaussian distribution se aaye hain. Gaussian ke parameters estimate karte waqt ye likely outliers ko ignore karta hai, isliye envelope ka estimation behtar hota hai aur outliers achhe se pakde jate hain.
  • Isolation forest: random forest banata hai jismein har tree randomly grow hota hai — har node par random feature aur random threshold se data ko split kiya jata hai, jab tak saare instances isolate na ho jayein. Anomalies doosre instances se door hoti hain, isliye wo kam steps mein isolate ho jati hain. High-dimensional datasets par bahut efficient hai.
  • Local outlier factor (LOF): kisi instance ke aas-paas ki density ko uske neighbors ke aas-paas ki density se compare karta hai. Anomaly aksar apne k-nearest neighbors se zyada isolated hoti hai.
  • One-class SVM: novelty detection ke liye behtar hai. Ye instances ko high-dimensional space mein origin se separate karne ki koshish karta hai, aur original space mein ek chhota region banata hai jo saare instances ko cover kare. Jo naya instance is region mein na aaye, wo anomaly hai. High-dimensional data par achha kaam karta hai, par bade datasets par scale nahi karta.
  • PCA reconstruction error: normal instance ka reconstruction error anomaly se usually bahut kam hota hai. Ye simple aur aksar kaafi efficient approach hai — jaise faces dataset par PCA se reconstruct karke modified images ka error bahut bada dikhta hai.
Yaad rakho: Anomaly detection mein threshold hi sab kuch hai — wo decide karta hai ki kitne false positives aur false negatives tum bardasht karoge. Apne use case ke hisaab se threshold ko tune karo, aur hamesha yaad rakho ki anomaly detection aur novelty detection mein training data ka assumption alag hota hai.

def plot_faces(faces, labels, n_cols=5):
    faces = faces.reshape(-1, 64, 64)
    n_rows = (len(faces) - 1) // n_cols + 1

    for index, (face, label) in enumerate(zip(faces, labels)):

        plt.imshow(face, cmap="gray")
        plt.axis("off")
        plt.title(label)
    plt.show()

def reconstruction_errors(pca, X):
    X_pca = pca.transform(X)
    X_reconstructed = pca.inverse_transform(X_pca)
    mse = np.square(X_reconstructed - X).mean(axis=-1)
    return mse

reconstruction_errors(pca, X_train).mean()

reconstruction_errors(pca, X_bad_faces).mean()

plot_faces(X_bad_faces, y_bad)

plot_faces(X_bad_faces_reconstructed, y_bad)

09Chapter 9 · Introduction to Artificial Neural Networks

Introduction to Artificial Neural Networks

Artificial neural network (ANN) matlab dimaag ki architecture se inspired machine learning model hai — lekin ye dimaag ki copy nahi hai. Jaise hawai-jahaaz panchhi se inspired hai par pankh nahi phadphadata, waise hi ANN biological neurons se inspired hai par bilkul waisa kaam nahi karta. ANN deep learning ke bilkul centre me hai: ye versatile, powerful aur scalable hai, isliye bade aur complex kaam — jaise arabon images classify karna, speech recognition, chatbot, video recommendation, ya protein folding — isse hote hain.

Biological neuron se artificial neuron tak

Biological neuron me cell body, dendrites aur ek lamba axon hota hai. Neuron ko kaafi chemical signals milen to wo khud ek electrical impulse bhejta hai. Akele neuron ka kaam simple lagta hai, lekin arabon neurons ke network se bahut complex computation ho jaata hai — jaise simple cheentiyon se complex anthill banta hai. Dimaag me neurons aksar consecutive layers me organize hote hain, khaas taur par cerebral cortex me.

ANN ka itihaas — teen lehren

  • 1943: pehla artificial neuron model aaya — binary inputs, binary output, aur ek threshold se upar jaane par neuron activate hota tha. Isse logical propositions compute kiye ja sakte the.
  • 1960s me girawat: bade waade poore nahi hue, funding kam hui, aur ANN ek lambe winter me chala gaya.
  • 1980s me wapsi: nayi architectures aur behtar training techniques aayi, lekin 1990s me support vector machines jaise techniques ne phir ANN ko peeche kar diya.
  • Aaj ki lehar: ye pehle se alag hai — bahut zyada data, GPU ki computing power, behtar training algorithms, aur 2017 me aaya Transformer architecture, jo text, image aur audio — sab process kar sakta hai aur bahut bade foundation models ko possible banata hai.

Aaj ki lehar pehle se alag kyun hai?

  • Data: train karne ke liye bahut zyada data available hai, aur bade complex problems par ANN aksar doosri techniques se behtar karta hai.
  • Compute: GPU — jo pehle graphics ke liye bane the — bade matrix multiplications ko fast karte hain, aur cloud se ye power sabko milti hai.
  • Behtar training: algorithms me chhote tweaks ne bada farq daala.
  • Local optima ka darr galat nikla: bade networks me local optima aksar global optimum jitne hi acche hote hain.
  • Transformer: ye scale hota hai, isliye bade foundation models bane jo transfer learning se ya sirf sahi prompt dekar (in-context learning, few-shot learning, chain-of-thought prompting) naye tasks kar lete hain.

Is chapter ka plan

Is chapter me pehle ANN architectures ka tour hoga, phir multilayer perceptron (MLP) tak jayenge — jo aaj bahut use hota hai. Scikit-learn se simple MLP banakar haath garam karenge, aur agle chapter me PyTorch par switch karenge, kyunki wo neural nets ke liye zyada flexible aur efficient hai.

Yaad rakho: ANN ko dimaag ki copy samajhna galti hai. Biological analogy se inspiration lo, lekin biologically realistic hone ki zid mat karo — jo kaam karta hai, wahi sahi hai.

09.1Chapter 9 · Introduction to Artificial Neural Networks

Perceptron aur MLP

Perceptron sabse simple ANN architecture me se ek hai. Iske peeche ek artificial neuron hota hai jise threshold logic unit (TLU) kehte hain: ye inputs ka weighted sum nikaalta hai, bias jodta hai, phir us par ek step function lagaata hai. Matlab z = w1*x1 + w2*x2 + ... + wn*xn + b, phir output = step(z).

Step function

Do common step functions hain: Heaviside step function (z < 0 par 0, z ≥ 0 par 1) aur sign function (z < 0 par -1, z = 0 par 0, z > 0 par +1). Ek TLU simple linear binary classification kar sakta hai — jaise petal length aur width se iris flower classify karna. Ye logistic regression jaisa lagta hai, farq sirf ye hai ki yahan logistic function ki jagah step function use hota hai.

Perceptron kya hai?

Perceptron ek layer me organize kiye gaye ek ya zyada TLUs se banta hai, jahan har TLU har input se connected hota hai. Aisi layer ko fully connected layer ya dense layer kehte hain. Inputs input layer banate hain, aur TLUs ki layer output layer hoti hai. Ek perceptron ek saath kai binary classes classify kar sakta hai (multilabel classifier), aur multiclass classification bhi kar sakta hai.

  • Layer ka computation: Y_hat = phi(XW + b) — X input matrix, W weight matrix, b bias vector, aur phi activation function hai. Broadcasting se bias har row me add hota hai.
  • Training rule: network ko ek-ek training instance diya jaata hai; jo output neuron galat predict kare, uske connection weights ko us direction me badhaya jaata hai jo sahi prediction me madad kare. Ye rule ek purane learning idea ka variant hai — jo connections error kam karte hain, wo mazboot hote hain.
  • Convergence: agar training instances linearly separable hain, to ye algorithm ek solution par converge karega.
  • Scikit-learn me: Perceptron class iris dataset par use hoti hai, aur ye SGDClassifier(loss="perceptron") ke barabar hai.

Perceptron ki limits

Har output neuron ki decision boundary linear hoti hai, isliye perceptron complex patterns nahi seekh sakta — bilkul logistic regression ki tarah. 1969 ki ek mashhoor book ne dikhaya ki perceptron kuch trivial problems bhi solve nahi kar sakta, jaise XOR classification problem. Isi disappointment ne kai logon ko neural networks se door kar diya.

MLP — perceptrons ko stack karo

Multiple perceptrons ko stack karne se multilayer perceptron (MLP) banta hai, jo XOR solve kar sakta hai. MLP me ek input layer, ek ya zyada hidden layers, aur ek output layer hoti hai. Input ke paas wali layers ko lower layers aur output ke paas wali ko upper layers kehte hain. Signal sirf ek direction me behta hai (input se output), isliye ye ek feedforward neural network hai. Jab hidden layers ka deep stack ho, to use deep neural network (DNN) kehte hain — deep learning isi ko study karta hai.

Yaad rakho: Perceptron logistic regression se isliye peeche hai kyunki wo class probability nahi deta, by default regularization use nahi karta, aur training tabhi ruk jaati hai jab training set par koi error na bache — isliye wo aksar utna generalize nahi karta.

import numpy as np
from sklearn.datasets import load_iris
from sklearn.linear_model import Perceptron

iris = load_iris(as_frame=True)
X = iris.data[["petal length (cm)", "petal width (cm)"]].values
y = (iris.target == 0)  # Iris setosa

per_clf = Perceptron(random_state=42)
per_clf.fit(X, y)

X_new = [[2, 0.5], [3, 1]]
y_pred = per_clf.predict(X_new)  # predicts True and False for these 2 flowers

y_pred

                        learning_rate="constant", eta0=1, random_state=42)
sgd_clf.fit(X, y)
assert (sgd_clf.coef_ == per_clf.coef_).all()
assert (sgd_clf.intercept_ == per_clf.intercept_).all()

plt.plot([axes[0], axes[1]], [a * axes[0] + b, a * axes[1] + b], "k-",

from scipy.special import expit as sigmoid

def relu(z):
    return np.maximum(0, z)

def derivative(f, z, eps=0.000001):
    return (f(z + eps) - f(z - eps)) / (2 * eps)

max_z = 2.5
z = np.linspace(-max_z, max_z, 200)

fig, axes = plt.subplots(nrows=2, ncols=4, figsize=(7, 3))

axes[0, 0].plot([-max_z, 0], [0, 0], "m-", linewidth=2)
axes[0, 0].plot(0, 0, "mx", markersize=7)
axes[0, 0].plot(0, 1, "mo", markersize=7)
axes[0, 0].plot([0, max_z], [1, 1], "m-", linewidth=2)
axes[0, 0].set_title("Heaviside", fontsize=12)
axes[1, 0].plot(z, derivative(np.sign, z), "m-", linewidth=2)
axes[1, 0].plot(0, 0, "mx", markersize=7)
axes[1, 0].set_ylabel("Derivative", fontsize=12)

axes[0, 1].plot(z, relu(z), "g-", linewidth=2)
axes[0, 1].set_title("ReLU", fontsize=12)
axes[1, 1].plot([-max_z, 0], [0, 0], "g-", linewidth=2)
axes[1, 1].plot([0, max_z], [1, 1], "g-", linewidth=2)
axes[1, 1].plot(0, 0, "gx", markersize=7)
axes[1, 1].plot(0, 1, "gx", markersize=7)

axes[0, 2].plot(z, sigmoid(z), "r-", linewidth=2)
axes[0, 2].set_title("Sigmoid", fontsize=12)
axes[1, 2].plot(z, derivative(sigmoid, z), "r-", linewidth=2)

axes[0, 3].plot(z, np.tanh(z), "b-", linewidth=1)
axes[0, 3].set_title("Tanh", fontsize=12)
axes[1, 3].plot(z, derivative(np.tanh, z), "b-", linewidth=1)

for row in range(2):
    for col in range(4):
        axes[row, col].grid(True)
        if row == 0:
            axes[row, col].set_xticklabels([])
        if col == 2:
            axes[row, col].set_xlim(-max_z, max_z)

        else:
            axes[row, col].set_xlim(-1.3, 1.3)

        if col != 0 and ((row, col) != (0, 3)):

        if (row, col) == (0, 3):

        else:
            axes[row, col].set_ylim(-0.5, 1.5)
            axes[row, col].set_yticks([0, 1])

plt.show()

← Previous09 · Introduction to Artificial Neural Networks→ Next09.2 · Activation Functions
09.2Chapter 9 · Introduction to Artificial Neural Networks

Activation Functions

Activation function wo nonlinearity hai jo har neuron ke weighted sum par lagti hai. Iske bina deep network ka koi fayda nahi: kai linear transformations ko chain karne se sirf ek aur linear transformation milta hai — jaise f(x) = 2x + 3 aur g(x) = 5x - 1 ko jodne se f(g(x)) = 10x + 1 milta hai. Nonlinearity ke bina deep stack ek hi layer ke barabar hota hai. Nonlinear activations ke saath kaafi bada DNN theoretically kisi bhi continuous function ko approximate kar sakta hai.

Sigmoid (logistic) function

sigmoid(z) = 1 / (1 + exp(-z)) — output 0 se 1 ke beech hota hai. Ye pehle MLPs me isliye zaroori thi kyunki step function ke flat segments par koi gradient nahi hota — gradient descent flat surface par move nahi kar sakta — jabki sigmoid ka derivative har jagah nonzero hota hai. Lekin sigmoid saturate hoti hai: bade positive ya negative inputs par derivative lagbhag 0 ho jaata hai.

Hyperbolic tangent (tanh)

tanh(z) = 2*sigmoid(2z) - 1 — S-shaped, continuous aur differentiable, lekin output -1 se 1 ke beech hota hai. Iska range output ko 0 ke aas-paas centred rakhta hai training ke shuru me, jo convergence ko aksar tez karta hai.

ReLU — aaj ka default

ReLU(z) = max(0, z) — continuous hai, lekin z = 0 par differentiable nahi hai, aur z < 0 par iska derivative 0 hota hai. Phir bhi practice me ye bahut accha kaam karta hai aur compute karne me fast hai, isliye ye zyada tar architectures ka default ban gaya hai (transformers ko chhodkar). Iska koi maximum output value nahi hota, jo gradient descent ke kuch issues ko kam karta hai.

Yaad rakho: Activation function sirf ek chhota sa function nahi hai — ye hi network ko nonlinear banata hai. Bina iske 100 layers bhi ek linear model ke barabar hain.

← Previous09.1 · Perceptron aur MLP→ Next09.3 · Backpropagation aur Training MLP (sklearn)
09.3Chapter 9 · Introduction to Artificial Neural Networks

Backpropagation aur Training MLP (sklearn)

MLP ko train karna saalon tak mushkil raha, jab tak ek efficient technique nahi mili: reverse-mode automatic differentiation (autodiff). Ye do passes me — ek forward, ek backward — network ke har parameter ke liye error ka gradient compute kar deta hai. Is combination ko — reverse-mode autodiff + gradient descent — backpropagation (backprop) kehte hain.

Backprop kaise kaam karta hai?

  • Forward pass: ek mini-batch (jaise 32 instances) ko network se guzaaro, har layer ka output compute karo, aur intermediate results save rakho. Ek poora training set pass karne ko ek epoch kehte hain.
  • Error measure karo: loss function se desired output aur actual output ka farq nikaalo.
  • Backward pass: chain rule se pehle output layer ke parameters ka error contribution nikaalo, phir peeche jaate hue har layer ke weights aur biases ka gradient measure karo.
  • Gradient descent step: in gradients se saare weights aur biases ko tweak karo taaki error kam ho.

Basketball wali analogy yaad rakho: ball phenko (forward pass), dekho kitni door gayi (error), socho body ko kaise adjust karein (backward pass), phir actually move karo (gradient descent step). Galti jitni chhoti, adjustment utna chhota.

Random initialization zaroori hai

Hidden layers ke saare weights ko randomly initialize karna zaroori hai. Agar sab weights aur biases zero rakho, to ek layer ke saare neurons bilkul identical rahenge, backprop unhe ek jaise hi affect karega, aur wo identical hi rahenge — matlab sau neurons hone par bhi model ek neuron jaisa behave karega. Random initialization is symmetry ko todta hai.

Regression MLP — sklearn se

Single value predict karni ho (jaise ghar ki keemat) to ek output neuron kaafi hai; multiple values ke liye har output dimension ke liye ek neuron chahiye. California housing dataset par MLPRegressor(hidden_layer_sizes=[50, 50, 50], early_stopping=True) + StandardScaler pipeline se 45 epochs me validation R2 lagbhag 0.79 aur test RMSE lagbhag 0.53 mila — random forest ke barabar. Hidden layers me ReLU use hoti hai, output layer par koi activation nahi hoti. Output ko positive rakhna ho to ReLU ya softplus, aur bounded rakhna ho to sigmoid ya tanh use karo. Loss ke liye MSE sahi hai; outliers zyada hon to Huber loss behtar hota hai, lekin MLPRegressor sirf MSE support karta hai.

Classification MLP — sklearn se

  • Binary: ek output neuron + sigmoid activation; output positive class ki probability hoti hai.
  • Multilabel binary: har label ke liye ek output neuron, sab par sigmoid; probabilities ka sum 1 hona zaroori nahi.
  • Multiclass: har class ke liye ek output neuron + poori output layer par softmax; probabilities 0–1 ke beech aur sum 1 hota hai. Loss ke liye cross-entropy use hoti hai.
  • Fashion MNIST: 70,000 grayscale images (28×28, 10 classes). MLPClassifier(hidden_layer_sizes=[300, 100]) + MinMaxScaler se test accuracy 89.3% mili. Pehli hidden layer me hi 784×300 + 300 = 235,500 parameters hote hain — isliye overfitting ka risk aur early stopping + L2 regularization zaroori hai.
  • Overconfidence se bacho: neural nets aksar galat hone par bhi 100% confident hote hain. Label smoothing madad karta hai — target class ki probability 1 se ghata kar 0.9 karo aur baaki 0.1 sab classes me baant do.

Hyperparameter guidelines

  • Hidden layers: ek hidden layer se shuru karo — kaafi neurons hon to wo complex functions model kar sakta hai. Lekin deep networks parameter-efficient hote hain: layers features ko reuse aur compose karte hain (pehli layer dots/lines, doosri shapes, teesri aankh/naak, upar wali face classify karti hai). MNIST par ek hidden layer se 97% se upar aur do se 98% se upar accuracy milti hai.
  • Neurons per layer: pehle pyramid shape (300, 200, 100) common tha, ab sab hidden layers me same neurons rakhna behtar mana jaata hai — sirf ek hyperparameter tune karna padta hai. Neurons badhate jao jab tak overfitting shuru na ho; bottleneck layer se bacho, kyunki wo useful information kho sakta hai.
  • Learning rate: optimal rate aksar maximum rate (jis par training diverge kare) ka aadha hota hai. Ek tareeka: bahut chhoti rate (10^-5) se shuru karke 500 iterations me 10 tak badhao, loss plot karo — loss jahan se upar chadhne lage, usse lagbhag 10 guna kam rate lo.
  • Batch size: bade batches GPU par efficient hote hain, lekin chhote batches (2 se 32) aksar behtar generalize karte hain. Bade batch + learning rate warmup bhi kaam karta hai (8,192 tak). Agar training unstable ho ya performance kharab ho, to chhota batch try karo.
  • Transfer learning: pehle se trained network ki lower layers reuse karo — naye task ko low-level structures dobara seekhne ki zaroorat nahi padti.
Yaad rakho: Scikit-learn me GPU acceleration nahi hai aur neural net features limited hain — isliye aage PyTorch use karenge. Lekin sklearn se kuch lines me MLP banana quick experiments ke liye bahut convenient hai.

10Chapter 10 · Building Neural Networks with PyTorch

Building Neural Networks with PyTorch

PyTorch ek powerful open-source deep learning library hai. Ye NumPy jaisa lagta hai, lekin isme hardware acceleration aur autodiff hai, plus optimizers aur ready-to-use neural net components milte hain. Iska sabse bada fayda hai dynamic computation graphs (define-by-run) — model ko Python code ki tarah likho, debug karo, loops aur conditionals use karo. Is chapter me tensors aur autograd se shuru karke linear regression, MLP, custom models, image classifier, hyperparameter tuning aur model export tak jayenge.

PyTorch kyun?

Jab PyTorch 2016 me aaya, tab ek doosri library sabse popular thi — fast aur scalable, lekin uska programming model complex aur static tha, use karna aur debug karna mushkil tha. PyTorch ne Pythonic, flexible approach diya, isliye researchers ne ise jaldi apna liya, aur phir industry bhi convert ho gayi. 2022 me iski governance PyTorch Foundation ko transfer ho gayi.

Is chapter ka plan

  • Tensors aur autograd: PyTorch ke core building blocks.
  • Linear regression: pehle tensors + autograd se, phir high-level API se.
  • MLP: regression aur classification, mini-batch training, evaluation.
  • Custom models: nonsequential models, multiple inputs aur outputs.
  • Fine-tuning aur export: Optuna se hyperparameters, model save/load, TorchScript aur compile.
Yaad rakho: PyTorch khud training loop nahi deta — tumhe khud likhna padta hai. Ye freedom aur control deta hai; agar ready-made loop chahiye to PyTorch Lightning, FastAI ya Keras jaise libraries dekho.

10.1Chapter 10 · Building Neural Networks with PyTorch

PyTorch Tensors

Tensor PyTorch ka core building block hai — ek multidimensional array jisme shape aur data type hota hai. Ye NumPy array jaisa hi hai, lekin do extra features hain: ye GPU (ya doosre hardware accelerators) par reh sakta hai, aur ye auto-differentiation support karta hai.

Tensor banana aur use karna

  • Create: torch.tensor([[1.0, 4.0, 7.0], [2.0, 3.0, 6.0]]) se 2×3 tensor banta hai. Ek tensor me sirf ek data type hota hai — float, integer, boolean ya complex. Strings ya objects support nahi hote.
  • Shape aur dtype: X.shape se torch.Size([2, 3]) aur X.dtype se torch.float32 milta hai.
  • Indexing: NumPy jaisi — X[0, 1], X[:, 1].
  • Operations: torch.abs(), torch.exp(), torch.mean(), torch.max(dim=0), matrix multiplication X @ X.T — sab NumPy jaisa API hai.
  • NumPy se convert: X.numpy() tensor ko NumPy array banata hai; torch.tensor(numpy_array, dtype=torch.float32) ulta karta hai. PyTorch me default float 32-bit hota hai (NumPy me 64-bit) — deep learning me 32-bit kaafi hai, aadhi RAM lagti hai aur compute fast hota hai.
  • Copy ya share: torch.tensor() aur torch.FloatTensor() copy banate hain; torch.from_numpy() data share karta hai — NumPy array badlo to tensor bhi badal jaata hai, aur vice versa.
  • In-place operations: naam ke end me underscore hota hai, jaise abs_(), sqrt_(), relu_() — ye memory bachate hain aur kabhi-kabhi tez hote hain.

Hardware acceleration — GPU par tensors

PyTorch Nvidia GPUs, Apple silicon (MPS), AMD GPUs (ROCm/DirectML), Intel GPUs/CPUs (oneAPI) aur Google TPUs (torch_xla library se) support karta hai. Device choose karo: torch.cuda.is_available() ho to "cuda", warna MPS, warna "cpu". Tensor ko GPU par bhejne ke liye M.to(device) use karo, ya seedha torch.tensor(..., device=device) se banao. Multiple GPUs hon to "cuda:0", "cuda:1" use karo.

  • Speed: 1000×1000 matrix multiplication par free Colab GPU ne CPU ke muqable 26× speedup diya (16.2 ms se 605 microseconds). Chhoti matrices par fayda kam hota hai — GPU bade kaam ko hazaaron cores me baant kar parallel chalata hai.
  • Data transfer se bacho: result bhi GPU par hi rehta hai, isliye kai operations bina CPU-GPU transfer ke ho jaate hain. Ye transfer aksar bottleneck banta hai.
  • Bina accelerator ke: deep learning bahut slow hoga — Colab ya Kaggle ke free GPU use karo.
Yaad rakho: Channel dimension ka dhyaan rakho — PyTorch me channels pehle hote hain ([batch, channels, height, width]), jabki Matplotlib, PIL aur TensorFlow me channels aakhir me hote hain. Galat order shape errors ki sabse common wajah hai.

10.2Chapter 10 · Building Neural Networks with PyTorch

Autograd aur Computation Graph

Autograd PyTorch ka reverse-mode auto-differentiation implementation hai — automatic gradients. Ye har forward pass me on-the-fly ek naya computation graph banata hai, isliye loops aur conditionals wale dynamic models bhi support hote hain.

Basic example — f(x) = x²

x = torch.tensor(5.0, requires_grad=True), phir f = x ** 2 se f = 25 milta hai aur f.backward() ke baad x.grad = 10 — jo derivative 2x ka sahi jawab hai.

  • requires_grad=True: batata hai ki x ek variable hai, constant nahi — PyTorch x se judi har operation track karega.
  • grad_fn: har result tensor par ye attribute hota hai jo batata hai ki use kis operation ne banaya (jaise PowBackward0) aur backprop me gradient kaise bhejna hai. Isi se computation graph banta hai.
  • backward(): gradients ko graph se peeche leaf nodes tak propagate karta hai.
  • grad: is attribute me computed derivative milta hai.

Gradient descent step — teen zaroori baatein

  • no_grad() context: gradient descent step ko with torch.no_grad(): ke andar karo — warna PyTorch khud us step ko bhi graph me track karne ki koshish karega aur error dega. Inference ke time bhi no_grad() use karo — kam RAM, tez kaam.
  • detach(): ek tensor ko graph se alag karta hai (requires_grad=False) lekin memory share rehti hai. Evaluation ya logging ke liye handy hai.
  • Gradients zero karo: har iteration se pehle x.grad.zero_() karo — warna backward() gradients ko accumulate karta rahega, aur galat updates milenge. Isme koi explicit error nahi aata, sirf kharab performance ya NaN values milte hain — debug karna mushkil hota hai.

In-place operations aur autograd — savdhaan

In-place operations autograd ke saath hamesha friendly nahi hoti. Leaf node (requires_grad=True wala tensor) par in-place operation karne se RuntimeError aata hai. Aur agar koi intermediate result in-place modify kar diya jo backward pass ko chahiye tha, to bhi RuntimeError aata hai — jaise z = t.exp(); z += 1; z.backward() fail hota hai, kyunki exp() apna output save karta hai gradient compute karne ke liye.

  • Output save karne wale ops: exp, relu, sigmoid, sqrt, tanh — inka output in-place modify mat karo.
  • Input save karne wale ops: abs, cos, log, sin, square — inka input in-place modify mat karo.
  • Dono save karne wale: max, min, norm, prod, std — na input na output modify karo.
  • Kuch nahi save karne wale: ceil, floor, mean, round, sum — inhe safely in-place modify kar sakte ho.
Yaad rakho: Pehle model bina in-place operations ke banao. Baad me memory ya speed ke liye kuch costly operations ko in-place banao — aur verify karo ki output same hai aur backprop abhi bhi chalta hai.
Poora code dekho — Autograd (Notebook 10, Ch 10)
python — Autograd — GitHub: https://github.com/ageron/handson-mlp/blob/main/10_neural_nets_with_pytorch.ipynb
x = torch.tensor(5.0, requires_grad=True)
f = x ** 2
f

f.backward()
x.grad

learning_rate = 0.1
with torch.no_grad():
    x -= learning_rate * x.grad  # gradient descent step

x

x_detached = x.detach()
x_detached -= learning_rate * x.grad

x.grad.zero_()

learning_rate = 0.1
x = torch.tensor(5.0, requires_grad=True)
for iteration in range(100):
    f = x ** 2  # forward pass
    f.backward()  # backward pass
    with torch.no_grad():
        x -= learning_rate * x.grad  # gradient descent step
    x.grad.zero_()  # reset the gradients

x

python — Linear regression implement karna — GitHub: https://github.com/ageron/handson-mlp/blob/main/10_neural_nets_with_pytorch.ipynb

    housing.data, housing.target, random_state=42)

    X_train_full, y_train_full, random_state=42)

X_valid = torch.FloatTensor(X_valid)
X_test = torch.FloatTensor(X_test)

X_train = (X_train - means) / stds
X_valid = (X_valid - means) / stds
X_test = (X_test - means) / stds

y_train = torch.FloatTensor(y_train).view(-1, 1)
y_valid = torch.FloatTensor(y_valid).view(-1, 1)
y_test = torch.FloatTensor(y_test).view(-1, 1)

torch.manual_seed(42)
n_features = X_train.shape[1]  # there are 8 input features
w = torch.randn((n_features, 1), requires_grad=True)
b = torch.tensor(0., requires_grad=True)

learning_rate = 0.4
n_epochs = 20
for epoch in range(n_epochs):
    y_pred = X_train @ w + b
    loss = ((y_pred - y_train) ** 2).mean()
    loss.backward()
    with torch.no_grad():
        b -= learning_rate * b.grad
        w -= learning_rate * w.grad
        b.grad.zero_()
        w.grad.zero_()
    print(f"Epoch {epoch + 1}/{n_epochs}, Loss: {loss.item()}")

X_new = X_test[:3]  # pretend these are new instances
with torch.no_grad():
    y_pred = X_new @ w + b  # use the trained parameters to make predictions

y_pred
