10.3Chapter 10 · Building Neural Networks with PyTorch

PyTorch se Regression aur Classification MLP

Ab fundamentals se asli models banate hain: pehle low-level tensors + autograd se linear regression, phir high-level API se, phir regression MLP, mini-batch training, evaluation, custom nonsequential models aur Fashion MNIST image classifier.

Linear regression — low-level

California housing data ko tensors me convert karo, mean/std se normalize karo, targets ko column vector (reshape(-1, 1)) banao. Weights w = torch.randn((8, 1), requires_grad=True) aur bias b banao, phir 20 epochs batch gradient descent chalao: y_pred = X_train @ w + b, MSE loss, loss.backward(), no_grad() me update, gradients zero karo. Loss 16.16 se girkar 0.57 hua. Reproducibility ke liye torch.manual_seed(42) use karo — lekin alag PyTorch version, platform ya device par results thode alag ho sakte hain.

High-level API — nn.Linear, optimizer, criterion

  • nn.Linear: nn.Linear(in_features=8, out_features=1) — ek module hai, nn.Module ka subclass. Iske weight aur bias nn.Parameter hote hain, jo normal tensor jaise use hote hain. Module ko function ki tarah call karne par forward() chalta hai.
  • Optimizer: torch.optim.SGD(model.parameters(), lr=...) — optimizer.step() update karta hai, optimizer.zero_grad() gradients zero karta hai.
  • Loss: nn.MSELoss() ko criterion kehte hain. Training loop ab chhota aur clean hai, aur loss 20 epochs me 0.54 tak gaya.
  • Hooks: register_forward_hook() se logging/debugging ke liye har call par function chalaya ja sakta hai. Model ko function ki tarah call karo, forward() ko seedha kabhi mat bulao.

Regression MLP aur mini-batch training

nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(8, 50), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(50, 40), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(40, 1)) — har layer ka output agle layer ka input hona chahiye. Mini-batch ke liye TensorDataset + DataLoader(batch_size=32, shuffle=True) use karo. Model ko model.to(device) se GPU par bhejo — aur optimizer ko model move karne ke BAAD banao, kyunki optimizer ki internal state model parameters wali device par allocate hoti hai. Training loop me model.train() se shuru karo; evaluation/prediction se pehle model.eval() karo. Speed ke liye CUDA par pin_memory=True aur num_workers (prefetching) use karo — lekin Windows par workers ka overhead kabhi training ko slow bhi kar deta hai, tab persistent_workers=True try karo.

Evaluation — batch metric wali galti se bacho

Har batch par RMSE compute karke unka mean lena poore set ka RMSE nahi hota (0.5732 vs sahi 0.6476). Sahi tareeka: metric ke liye MSE use karo aur aggregate function se uska square root lo. Ya TorchMetrics library ki streaming metrics use karo — torchmetrics.MeanSquaredError(squared=False) update karte jao, ant me compute() karo.

Custom models — Wide & Deep, multiple inputs/outputs

  • Wide & Deep: deep path (MLP stack) ke saath ek short path bhi hota hai jo inputs ko seedha output layer se jodta hai — deep patterns aur simple rules dono seekhe ja sakte hain, aur manually engineered features bhi diye ja sakte hain. Custom module banao: nn.Module se inherit karo, constructor me layers banao, forward() me unhe use karo.
  • Multiple inputs: alag-alag tensors (jaise images + text) ek tensor me combine nahi ho sakte. forward(self, X_wide, X_deep) likho, aur dataset se alag-alag tensors lo. Input order galat hone se mushkil bugs aate hain — isliye named inputs wala custom Dataset banao jo dictionary return kare, aur model(**inputs) se call karo.
  • Multiple outputs: ek model se kai tasks — jaise picture me object locate karna (regression) + classify karna — ya auxiliary output se regularization. Har output ka loss nikaalo, phir weighted sum banao (jaise 0.8 * main_loss + 0.2 * aux_loss). Evaluation me auxiliary output ko ignore kar sakte ho.

Image classifier — Fashion MNIST

TorchVision se dataset load karo: torchvision.datasets.FashionMNIST + transforms (ToImage, phir ToDtype(torch.float32, scale=True)) se PIL images ko 0–1 range ke float tensors me badlo. Har image ka shape [1, 28, 28] hota hai — channel pehle. 60,000 training images me se 5,000 validation ke liye alag karo (random_split).

  • Model: nn.Flatten() (batch [32, 1, 28, 28] ko [32, 784] banata hai), phir Linear(784, 300), ReLU, Linear(300, 100), ReLU, Linear(100, 10). Output layer par koi activation nahi — model logits deta hai.
  • Loss: nn.CrossEntropyLoss logits se seedha cross-entropy compute karta hai — tez aur numerically stable. Probabilities chahiye to F.softmax(logits, dim=1) manually lagao. Binary ke liye BCEWithLogitsLoss, multilabel ke liye har label par ek neuron. Label smoothing ke liye label_smoothing argument hai.
  • Results: training accuracy lagbhag 92.8%, validation 87.6% — thodi overfitting hai, regularization chahiye (Chapter 11). Top-k predictions ke liye torch.topk() use karo. Unbalanced dataset ho to CrossEntropyLoss ka weight argument se rare classes ko zyada weight do.
Yaad rakho: model.train() aur model.eval() bhoolna sabse common galti hai — Dropout aur BatchNorm jaise layers in modes me alag behave karte hain (Chapter 11 me detail).

def train(model, optimizer, criterion, train_loader, n_epochs):
    model.train()
    for epoch in range(n_epochs):
        total_loss = 0.
        for X_batch, y_batch in train_loader:
            X_batch, y_batch = X_batch.to(device), y_batch.to(device)
            y_pred = model(X_batch)
            loss = criterion(y_pred, y_batch)
            total_loss += loss.item()
            loss.backward()
            optimizer.step()
            optimizer.zero_grad()

        mean_loss = total_loss / len(train_loader)
        print(f"Epoch {epoch + 1}/{n_epochs}, Loss: {mean_loss:.4f}")

def evaluate(model, data_loader, metric_fn, aggregate_fn=torch.mean):
    model.eval()
    metrics = []
    with torch.no_grad():
        for X_batch, y_batch in data_loader:
            X_batch, y_batch = X_batch.to(device), y_batch.to(device)
            y_pred = model(X_batch)
            metric = metric_fn(y_pred, y_batch)
            metrics.append(metric)
    return aggregate_fn(torch.stack(metrics))

def rmse(y_pred, y_true):
    return ((y_pred - y_true) ** 2).mean().sqrt()

evaluate(model, valid_loader, rmse)

valid_mse.sqrt()

evaluate(model, valid_loader, mse,
         aggregate_fn=lambda metrics: torch.sqrt(torch.mean(metrics)))

import torchmetrics

def evaluate_tm(model, data_loader, metric):
    model.eval()
    metric.reset()  # reset the metric at the beginning
    with torch.no_grad():
        for X_batch, y_batch in data_loader:
            X_batch, y_batch = X_batch.to(device), y_batch.to(device)
            y_pred = model(X_batch)
            metric.update(y_pred, y_batch)  # update it at each iteration
    return metric.compute()  # compute the final result at the end

rmse = torchmetrics.MeanSquaredError(squared=False).to(device)
evaluate_tm(model, valid_loader, rmse)

def train2(model, optimizer, criterion, metric, train_loader, valid_loader,
               n_epochs):
    history = {"train_losses": [], "train_metrics": [], "valid_metrics": []}
    for epoch in range(n_epochs):
        total_loss = 0.
        metric.reset()
        for X_batch, y_batch in train_loader:
            model.train()
            X_batch, y_batch = X_batch.to(device), y_batch.to(device)
            y_pred = model(X_batch)
            loss = criterion(y_pred, y_batch)
            total_loss += loss.item()
            loss.backward()
            optimizer.step()
            optimizer.zero_grad()
            metric.update(y_pred, y_batch)
        mean_loss = total_loss / len(train_loader)
        history["train_losses"].append(mean_loss)
        history["train_metrics"].append(metric.compute().item())
        history["valid_metrics"].append(
            evaluate_tm(model, valid_loader, metric).item())
        print(f"Epoch {epoch + 1}/{n_epochs}, "
              f"train loss: {history['train_losses'][-1]:.4f}, "
              f"train metric: {history['train_metrics'][-1]:.4f}, "
              f"valid metric: {history['valid_metrics'][-1]:.4f}")
    return history

class WideAndDeep(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, n_features):
        super().__init__()
        self.deep_stack = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(n_features, 50), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(50, 40), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(40, 30), nn.ReLU(),
        )
        self.output_layer = nn.Linear(30 + n_features, 1)

    def forward(self, X):
        deep_output = self.deep_stack(X)
        wide_and_deep = torch.concat([X, deep_output], dim=1)
        return self.output_layer(wide_and_deep)

class WideAndDeepV2(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, n_features):
        super().__init__()
        self.deep_stack = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(n_features - 2, 50), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(50, 40), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(40, 30), nn.ReLU(),
        )
        self.output_layer = nn.Linear(30 + 5, 1)

    def forward(self, X):
        X_wide = X[:, :5]
        X_deep = X[:, 2:]
        deep_output = self.deep_stack(X_deep)
        wide_and_deep = torch.concat([X_wide, deep_output], dim=1)
        return self.output_layer(wide_and_deep)

class WideAndDeepV3(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, n_features):
        super().__init__()
        self.deep_stack = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(n_features - 2, 50), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(50, 40), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(40, 30), nn.ReLU(),
        )
        self.output_layer = nn.Linear(30 + 5, 1)

    def forward(self, X_wide, X_deep):
        deep_output = self.deep_stack(X_deep)
        wide_and_deep = torch.concat([X_wide, deep_output], dim=1)
        return self.output_layer(wide_and_deep)

torch.manual_seed(42)
train_data_wd = TensorDataset(X_train[:, :5], X_train[:, 2:], y_train)
train_loader_wd = DataLoader(train_data_wd, batch_size=32, shuffle=True)
valid_data_wd = TensorDataset(X_valid[:, :5], X_valid[:, 2:], y_valid)

def evaluate_multi_in(model, data_loader, metric):
    model.eval()
    metric.reset()  # reset the metric at the beginning
    with torch.no_grad():
        for X_batch_wide, X_batch_deep, y_batch in data_loader:
            X_batch_wide = X_batch_wide.to(device)
            X_batch_deep = X_batch_deep.to(device)
            y_batch = y_batch.to(device)
            y_pred = model(X_batch_wide, X_batch_deep)
            metric.update(y_pred, y_batch)  # update it at each iteration
    return metric.compute()  # compute the final result at the end

def train_multi_in(model, optimizer, criterion, metric, train_loader,
                   valid_loader, n_epochs):
    history = {"train_losses": [], "train_metrics": [], "valid_metrics": []}
    for epoch in range(n_epochs):
        total_loss = 0.
        metric.reset()
        for *X_batch_inputs, y_batch in train_loader:
            model.train()
            X_batch_inputs = [X.to(device) for X in X_batch_inputs]
            y_batch = y_batch.to(device)
            y_pred = model(*X_batch_inputs)
            loss = criterion(y_pred, y_batch)
            total_loss += loss.item()
            loss.backward()
            optimizer.step()
            optimizer.zero_grad()
            metric.update(y_pred, y_batch)
        mean_loss = total_loss / len(train_loader)
        history["train_losses"].append(mean_loss)
        history["train_metrics"].append(metric.compute().item())
        history["valid_metrics"].append(
            evaluate_multi_in(model, valid_loader, metric).item())
        print(f"Epoch {epoch + 1}/{n_epochs}, "
              f"train loss: {history['train_losses'][-1]:.4f}, "
              f"train metric: {history['train_metrics'][-1]:.4f}, "
              f"valid metric: {history['valid_metrics'][-1]:.4f}")
    return history

class WideAndDeepDataset(torch.utils.data.Dataset):
    def __init__(self, X_wide, X_deep, y):
        self.X_wide = X_wide
        self.X_deep = X_deep
        self.y = y

    def __len__(self):
        return len(self.y)

    def __getitem__(self, idx):
        input_dict = {"X_wide": self.X_wide[idx], "X_deep": self.X_deep[idx]}
        return input_dict, self.y[idx]

def evaluate_named(model, data_loader, metric):
    model.eval()
    metric.reset()  # reset the metric at the beginning
    with torch.no_grad():
        for inputs, y_batch in data_loader:
            inputs = {name: X.to(device) for name, X in inputs.items()}
            y_batch = y_batch.to(device)
            y_pred = model(X_wide=inputs["X_wide"], X_deep=inputs["X_deep"])
            metric.update(y_pred, y_batch)
    return metric.compute()  # compute the final result at the end

def train_named(model, optimizer, criterion, metric, train_loader,
                   valid_loader, n_epochs):
    history = {"train_losses": [], "train_metrics": [], "valid_metrics": []}
    for epoch in range(n_epochs):
        total_loss = 0.
        metric.reset()
        for inputs, y_batch in train_loader:
            model.train()
            inputs = {name: X.to(device) for name, X in inputs.items()}
            y_batch = y_batch.to(device)
            y_pred = model(**inputs)
            loss = criterion(y_pred, y_batch)
            total_loss += loss.item()
            loss.backward()
            optimizer.step()
            optimizer.zero_grad()
            metric.update(y_pred, y_batch)
        mean_loss = total_loss / len(train_loader)
        history["train_losses"].append(mean_loss)
        history["train_metrics"].append(metric.compute().item())
        history["valid_metrics"].append(
            evaluate_named(model, valid_loader, metric).item())
        print(f"Epoch {epoch + 1}/{n_epochs}, "
              f"train loss: {history['train_losses'][-1]:.4f}, "
              f"train metric: {history['train_metrics'][-1]:.4f}, "
              f"valid metric: {history['valid_metrics'][-1]:.4f}")
    return history

python — Multiple outputs wale models — GitHub: https://github.com/ageron/handson-mlp/blob/main/10_neural_nets_with_pytorch.ipynb
class WideAndDeepV4(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, n_features):
        super().__init__()
        self.deep_stack = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(n_features - 2, 50), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(50, 40), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(40, 30), nn.ReLU(),
        )
        self.output_layer = nn.Linear(30 + 5, 1)
        self.aux_output_layer = nn.Linear(30, 1)

    def forward(self, X_wide, X_deep):
        deep_output = self.deep_stack(X_deep)
        wide_and_deep = torch.concat([X_wide, deep_output], dim=1)
        main_output = self.output_layer(wide_and_deep)
        aux_output = self.aux_output_layer(deep_output)
        return main_output, aux_output

import torchmetrics

def evaluate_multi_out(model, data_loader, metric):
    model.eval()
    metric.reset()
    with torch.no_grad():
        for inputs, y_batch in data_loader:
            inputs = {name: X.to(device) for name, X in inputs.items()}
            y_batch = y_batch.to(device)
            y_pred, _ = model(**inputs)
            metric.update(y_pred, y_batch)
    return metric.compute()

def train_multi_out(model, optimizer, criterion, metric, train_loader,
                   valid_loader, n_epochs):
    history = {"train_losses": [], "train_metrics": [], "valid_metrics": []}
    for epoch in range(n_epochs):
        total_loss = 0.
        metric.reset()
        for inputs, y_batch in train_loader:
            model.train()
            inputs = {name: X.to(device) for name, X in inputs.items()}
            y_batch = y_batch.to(device)
            y_pred, y_pred_aux = model(**inputs)
            main_loss = criterion(y_pred, y_batch)
            aux_loss = criterion(y_pred_aux, y_batch)
            loss = 0.8 * main_loss + 0.2 * aux_loss
            total_loss += loss.item()
            loss.backward()
            optimizer.step()
            optimizer.zero_grad()
            metric.update(y_pred, y_batch)
        mean_loss = total_loss / len(train_loader)
        history["train_losses"].append(mean_loss)
        history["train_metrics"].append(metric.compute().item())
        history["valid_metrics"].append(
            evaluate_multi_out(model, valid_loader, metric).item())
        print(f"Epoch {epoch + 1}/{n_epochs}, "
              f"train loss: {history['train_losses'][-1]:.4f}, "
              f"train metric: {history['train_metrics'][-1]:.4f}, "
              f"valid metric: {history['valid_metrics'][-1]:.4f}")
    return history

torch.manual_seed(42)
learning_rate = 0.01
model = WideAndDeepV4(n_features).to(device)
optimizer = torch.optim.SGD(model.parameters(), lr=learning_rate, momentum=0)
mse = nn.MSELoss()
rmse = torchmetrics.MeanSquaredError(squared=False).to(device)
history = train_multi_out(model, optimizer, mse, rmse, train_loader_named,
                          valid_loader_named, n_epochs)

python — Classifier banana — GitHub: https://github.com/ageron/handson-mlp/blob/main/10_neural_nets_with_pytorch.ipynb
class ImageClassifier(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, n_inputs, n_hidden1, n_hidden2, n_classes):
        super().__init__()
        self.mlp = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Flatten(),
            nn.Linear(n_inputs, n_hidden1),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(n_hidden1, n_hidden2),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(n_hidden2, n_classes)
        )

    def forward(self, X):
        return self.mlp(X)

10.4Chapter 10 · Building Neural Networks with PyTorch

Fine-tuning, Optuna aur Model Export

Model ban gaya, train ho gaya — ab use behtar banao, save karo aur production me bhejne layak banao. Manual tuning ke alawa automatic hyperparameter search bhi hai, aur model ko save karne ke kai tareeke hain — har ek ke apne trade-offs.

Optuna se hyperparameter tuning

Optuna ek dedicated fine-tuning library hai (doosre options: Ray Tune, Hyperopt). Ek objective(trial) function likho jo trial se hyperparameter values maange (trial.suggest_float("learning_rate", 1e-5, 1e-1, log=True), trial.suggest_int("n_hidden", 20, 300)), model banakar train kare, aur validation metric return kare. Phir study = optuna.create_study(direction="maximize") aur study.optimize(objective, n_trials=5) chalao. Optuna TPE algorithm use karta hai — pehle random values try karta hai, phir past results se seekhkar promising regions par focus karta hai, isliye random search se behtar hai.

  • 5 trials bahut kam hain: example me best learning rate 0.0085 aur n_hidden 188 mila, validation accuracy 85.5% — pehle wale manual result se kharab, kyunki sirf 5 trials the. 50 ya zyada trials se bahut behtar milega, lekin ghanton lagega.
  • Pruning: kharab trials ko jaldi roko — trial.report(accuracy, epoch) ke baad trial.should_prune() true ho to optuna.TrialPruned raise karo. MedianPruner median se neeche performance wale trials ko prune karta hai.
  • Parallel trials: SQL database (SQLite/PostgreSQL) + study_name + load_if_exists=True se kai machines par parallel chala sakte ho — near-linear speedup milta hai.
  • Search space savdhaan: har naya hyperparameter search space ko exponentially bada karta hai — sirf wahi add karo jo worth ho.

Model save aur load karna

  • Poora model: torch.save(model, "model.pt") aur torch.load("model.pt", weights_only=False) — simple hai, lekin pickle insecure hai (malicious code run ho sakta hai) aur Python version/folder structure par brittle hai. Custom classes ka code load karne se pehle environment me hona chahiye.
  • Sirf weights (recommended): torch.save(model.state_dict(), "weights.pt") — state dict sirf data hota hai, isliye safe hai. Load karne ke liye pehle wahi architecture banao, phir torch.load(..., weights_only=True) aur load_state_dict() karo. Hyperparameters bhi saath save karo taaki architecture dobara ban sake.
  • Training resume karni ho: optimizer ka state dict, current epoch aur loss history bhi save karo.
  • safetensors: ek aur popular safe tareeka hai weights save karne ka.

Compile aur optimize — TorchScript aur torch.compile

  • TorchScript: model ko statically typed Python subset me convert karta hai — operations fuse hote hain, constants fold hote hain, unused code prune hota hai — inference tez hoti hai aur model C++ (LibTorch) me bhi chal sakta hai. torch.jit.trace(model, X_new) sample data se operations log karta hai — lekin if/loops wale dynamic models ke liye sahi nahi (sirf executed branch capture hoti hai). torch.jit.script(model) code ko parse karta hai — if/while support karta hai, lekin Python ka sirf ek subset allowed hai.
  • torch.compile: PyTorch 2.0 se ye naya tareeka hai — compiled_model = torch.compile(model) se JIT compilation hoti hai, jo conditionals aur loops ko sahi handle karta hai. TorchScript ab actively develop nahi ho raha — bugs fix hote hain, naye features nahi.
  • ONNX: torch.onnx.export() se open ONNX standard me export karke kai environments me inference kar sakte ho.
Yaad rakho: Hyperparameters final hone ke baad model ko full training set (training + validation) par dobara train karo, phir test set par evaluate karo — aur tabhi save karke production me bhejo.

import optuna

def objective(trial):
    learning_rate = trial.suggest_float("learning_rate", 1e-5, 1e-1, log=True)
    n_hidden = trial.suggest_int("n_hidden", 20, 300)
    model = ImageClassifier(n_inputs=1 * 28 * 28, n_hidden1=n_hidden,
                            n_hidden2=n_hidden, n_classes=10).to(device)
    optimizer = torch.optim.SGD(model.parameters(), lr=learning_rate)
    xentropy = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
    accuracy = torchmetrics.Accuracy(task="multiclass", num_classes=10)
    accuracy = accuracy.to(device)
    history = train2(model, optimizer, xentropy, accuracy, train_loader,
                     valid_loader, n_epochs=10)
    validation_accuracy = max(history["valid_metrics"])
    return validation_accuracy

torch.manual_seed(42)
sampler = optuna.samplers.TPESampler(seed=42)
study = optuna.create_study(direction="maximize", sampler=sampler)
study.optimize(objective, n_trials=5)

study.best_params

study.best_value

def objective(trial, train_loader, valid_loader):
    learning_rate = trial.suggest_float("learning_rate", 1e-5, 1e-1, log=True)
    n_hidden = trial.suggest_int("n_hidden", 20, 300)
    model = ImageClassifier(n_inputs=1 * 28 * 28, n_hidden1=n_hidden,
                            n_hidden2=n_hidden, n_classes=10).to(device)
    optimizer = torch.optim.SGD(model.parameters(), lr=learning_rate)
    xentropy = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
    accuracy = torchmetrics.Accuracy(task="multiclass", num_classes=10)
    accuracy = accuracy.to(device)
    best_validation_accuracy = 0.0
    for epoch in range(n_epochs):
        history = train2(model, optimizer, xentropy, accuracy, train_loader,
                         valid_loader, n_epochs=1)
        validation_accuracy = max(history["valid_metrics"])
        if validation_accuracy > best_validation_accuracy:
            best_validation_accuracy = validation_accuracy
        trial.report(validation_accuracy, epoch)
        if trial.should_prune():
            raise optuna.TrialPruned()
    return best_validation_accuracy

objective_with_data = lambda trial: objective(
    trial, train_loader=train_loader, valid_loader=valid_loader)

from functools import partial

objective_with_data = partial(objective, train_loader=train_loader,
                              valid_loader=valid_loader)

torch.manual_seed(42)
sampler = optuna.samplers.TPESampler(seed=42)
pruner = optuna.pruners.MedianPruner()
study = optuna.create_study(direction="maximize", sampler=sampler,
                            pruner=pruner)
study.optimize(objective_with_data, n_trials=20)

study.best_value

study.best_params

class Dense(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, in_features, out_features):
        super().__init__()
        self.linear = nn.Linear(in_features, out_features)
        self.relu = nn.ReLU()

    def forward(self, X):
        return self.relu(self.linear(X))

torch.manual_seed(42)
dense = Dense(3, 5)
X = torch.randn(2, 3)
y_pred = dense(X)
y_pred.shape

y_pred_check = dense.relu(X @ dense.linear.weight.T + dense.linear.bias)
torch.allclose(y_pred, y_pred_check)

class Dense2(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, in_features, out_features):
        super().__init__()
        self.weight = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(out_features, in_features))
        self.bias = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(out_features))

    def forward(self, X):
        z = X @ self.weight.T + self.bias
        return F.relu(z)

torch.manual_seed(42)
dense2 = Dense2(3, 5)
X = torch.randn(2, 3)
y_pred2 = dense2(X)
y_pred2.shape

y_pred2_check = F.relu(X @ dense2.weight.T + dense2.bias)
torch.allclose(y_pred2, y_pred2_check)

class Dense3(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, in_features, out_features):
        super().__init__()
        self.weight = nn.Parameter(torch.empty(out_features, in_features))
        nn.init.kaiming_uniform_(self.weight, nonlinearity="relu")
        self.bias = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(out_features))

    def forward(self, X):
        z = X @ self.weight.T + self.bias
        return F.relu(z)

torch.manual_seed(42)

X = torch.randn(2, 3)

y_pred3_check = F.relu(X @ dense3.weight.T + dense3.bias)
torch.allclose(y_pred3, y_pred3_check)

class CoverTypeModel(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, n_neurons, n_inputs=n_inputs, n_classes=n_classes):
        super().__init__()
        layers = [
            Dense3(n_in, n_out)
            for n_in, n_out in zip([n_inputs] + n_neurons, n_neurons)
        ] + [nn.Linear(n_neurons[-1], n_classes)]
        self.mlp = nn.Sequential(*layers)

    def forward(self, X):
        return self.mlp(X)

torch.manual_seed(42)
covtype_model = CoverTypeModel([200, 100, 50]).to(device)

class CoverTypeModel(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, n_neurons, n_inputs=n_inputs, n_classes=n_classes):
        super().__init__()
        layers = [
            Dense3(n_in, n_out)
            for n_in, n_out in zip([n_inputs] + n_neurons, n_neurons)
        ] + [nn.Linear(n_neurons[-1], n_classes)]
        self.layers = nn.ModuleList(layers)

    def forward(self, X):
        for layer in self.layers:
            X = layer(X)
        return X

torch.manual_seed(42)
covtype_model = CoverTypeModel([200, 100, 50]).to(device)

for learning_rate in [0.16, 0.08, 0.04, 0.02, 0.01, 0.005]:

def objective(trial):
    learning_rate = trial.suggest_float("learning_rate", 1e-2, 1.0, log=True)
    n_layers = trial.suggest_int("n_layers", 1, 3)
    n_hidden = trial.suggest_int("n_hidden", 30, 150)
    covtype_model = CoverTypeModel([n_hidden] * n_layers).to(device)
    optimizer = torch.optim.SGD(covtype_model.parameters(), lr=learning_rate)
    xentropy = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
    accuracy = torchmetrics.Accuracy(task="multiclass",
                                     num_classes=n_classes).to(device)
    best_validation_accuracy = 0.0
    for epoch in range(n_epochs):
        history = train2(covtype_model, optimizer, xentropy, accuracy,
                         train_loader, valid_loader, n_epochs=1)
        validation_accuracy = max(history["valid_metrics"])
        if validation_accuracy > best_validation_accuracy:
            best_validation_accuracy = validation_accuracy
        trial.report(validation_accuracy, step=epoch)
        if trial.should_prune():
            raise optuna.TrialPruned()
    return best_validation_accuracy

torch.manual_seed(42)
sampler = optuna.samplers.TPESampler(seed=42)
pruner = optuna.pruners.MedianPruner()
study = optuna.create_study(direction="maximize", sampler=sampler,
                            pruner=pruner)
study.optimize(objective, n_trials=2)

study.best_value

11Chapter 11 · Training Deep Neural Networks

Training Deep Neural Networks

Chapter 10 me tumne shallow nets banaye — sirf kuch hidden layers. Lekin complex problem ke liye, jaise high-resolution images me sainkadon types ke objects detect karna, tumhe dozens ya sainkadon layers chahiye honge, har layer me sainkadon neurons, lakhon connections. Aise deep network ko train karna aasan nahi hai.

Deep nets train karte time chaar badi problems

  • Unstable gradients: backprop me gradients neeche jaate-jaate bahut chhote (vanishing) ya bahut bade (exploding) ho jaate hain — lower layers train hi nahi hoti.
  • Kam labeled data: bade network ke liye kaafi labeled data nahi hota, ya labeling bahut mehenga hota hai.
  • Slow training: training bahut zyada slow ho sakta hai.
  • Overfitting: lakhon parameters wala model training set ko ratne lagta hai, khaas taur par jab data kam ya noisy ho.

Is chapter ka roadmap

  • Gradients: vanishing/exploding gradients, smart initialization, behtar activation functions, batch-norm, layer-norm, gradient clipping.
  • Kam data: transfer learning aur unsupervised pretraining.
  • Speed: tez optimizers aur learning rate scheduling.
  • Overfitting: L1/L2 regularization, dropout, MC dropout, max-norm regularization.
Yaad rakho: Ye chapter ek toolkit hai — har technique har problem ke liye nahi hai. Chapter ke ant me default configuration di gayi hai jo zyada tar cases me bina zyada tuning ke kaam karti hai.

11.1Chapter 11 · Training Deep Neural Networks

Vanishing aur Exploding Gradients

Backprop output layer se input layer ki taraf error gradient propagate karta hai. Problem ye hai ki gradients aksar neeche jaate-jaate chhote hote jaate hain — lower layers ke weights lagbhag badalte hi nahi, aur training kabhi acche solution par converge nahi karti. Ise vanishing gradients problem kehte hain. Ulta bhi ho sakta hai: gradients bade hote jaayein, weights ko insanely bade updates milen, aur algorithm diverge kar jaaye — ye exploding gradients problem hai, jo recurrent neural networks me sabse zyada dikhti hai.

Aisa hota kyun hai? — sigmoid + galat initialization

Ek mashhoor 2010 ke study ne dikhaya ki sigmoid activation function aur us time ki popular initialization (mean 0, standard deviation 1 wali normal distribution) ke combination se har layer ke outputs ki variance inputs se bahut zyada ho jaati hai. Aage badhte hue variance badhti jaati hai jab tak activation function top layers me saturate na ho jaaye. Sigmoid ka mean 0.5 hota hai (0 nahi), jo saturation ko aur badhata hai — tanh ka mean 0 hota hai, isliye wo deep networks me thoda behtar behave karti hai.

  • Saturation: sigmoid ke inputs bade (positive ya negative) hone par function 0 ya 1 par saturate ho jaata hai aur derivative lagbhag 0 ho jaata hai — backprop ke paas propagate karne ke liye gradient hi nahi bachta.
  • Dilution: jo chhota sa gradient bachta hai, wo top layers se guzarte hue aur dilute hota jaata hai — lower layers tak kuch nahi pahunchta.
  • Asar: alag-alag layers alag speeds par seekhte hain — deep networks unstable ho jaate hain. Yehi wajah thi ki 2000s ke shuru me deep networks ko mostly chhod diya gaya tha.

Signal ko dono directions me sahi behna chahiye

Solution ka core idea simple hai: signal ko forward direction (predictions) aur reverse direction (gradients) dono me sahi se behna chahiye — na marna chahiye, na explode hona chahiye. Iske liye har layer ke outputs ki variance inputs ki variance ke barabar honi chahiye, aur gradients ki variance bhi layer se guzarne se pehle aur baad me barabar honi chahiye. Dono ek saath guarantee karna tabhi possible hai jab layer ke inputs aur outputs ki sankhya barabar ho — isliye ek practical compromise use hota hai (agle section me).

Yaad rakho: Vanishing gradients ka matlab ye nahi ki network kuch seekh hi nahi raha — upar wali layers tez seekhti hain, neeche wali atak jaati hain. Isliye deep net ki training curves me lambi plateaus dikhte hain.
Poora code dekho — Vanishing/exploding gradients problem (Notebook 11, Ch 11)
python — Vanishing/exploding gradients problem — GitHub: https://github.com/ageron/handson-mlp/blob/main/11_training_deep_neural_networks.ipynb
# extra code – this cell generates Figure 11–1

import numpy as np

def sigmoid(z):
    return 1 / (1 + np.exp(-z))

z = np.linspace(-5, 5, 200)

plt.plot([-5, 5], [0, 0], 'k-')
plt.plot([-5, 5], [1, 1], 'k--')
plt.plot([0, 0], [-0.2, 1.2], 'k-')
plt.plot([-5, 5], [-3/4, 7/4], 'g--')
plt.plot(z, sigmoid(z), "b-", linewidth=2,
         label=r"$\sigma(z) = \dfrac{1}{1+e^{-z}}$")
props = dict(facecolor='black', shrink=0.1)
plt.annotate('Saturating', xytext=(3.5, 0.7), xy=(5, 1), arrowprops=props,
             fontsize=14, ha="center")
plt.annotate('Saturating', xytext=(-3.5, 0.3), xy=(-5, 0), arrowprops=props,
             fontsize=14, ha="center")
plt.annotate('Linear', xytext=(2, 0.2), xy=(0, 0.5), arrowprops=props,
             fontsize=14, ha="center")
plt.grid(True)
plt.axis([-5, 5, -0.2, 1.2])
plt.xlabel("$z$")
plt.legend(loc="upper left", fontsize=16)

plt.show()

11.2Chapter 11 · Training Deep Neural Networks

Initialization aur Activation ki Choice

Unstable gradients ka ek bada ilaaj hai weights ko sahi scale se initialize karna — aur sahi activation function chunna. Dono ek-doosre se jude hain: har activation function ke liye alag initialization scale sahi hota hai.

Initialization — variance ko stable rakho

  • Sigmoid/tanh/softmax ke liye: weights ko mean 0 wali distribution se is scale par initialize karo ki variance = 1 / fan_avg ho, jahan fan_avg = (fan_in + fan_out) / 2 hai. Fan-in matlab layer ke inputs ki sankhya, fan-out matlab outputs ki sankhya. Uniform distribution ke liye range ±sqrt(3 / fan_avg) hoti hai.
  • ReLU aur uske variants (leaky ReLU, ELU, GELU, Swish, Mish) ke liye: variance = 2 / fan_in use karo — ReLU aadhe inputs ko zero kar deta hai, isliye variance double chahiye.
  • SELU ke liye: variance = 1 / fan_in wali initialization use karo, preferably normal distribution se.
  • PyTorch me: nn.Linear ki default initialization optimal scale se kam hoti hai. Sahi tareeka: torch.nn.init module ke functions use karo — jaise torch.nn.init module ke ReLU ke liye wale uniform initialization function aur nn.init.zeros_(layer.bias). Poore model par lagane ke liye ek function likho jo nn.Linear layers ko check kare, aur model.apply(...) se apply karo.
  • Orthogonal initialization: random orthogonal matrix se initialize karo — ye norms preserve karta hai, isliye activations aur gradients stable rehte hain. Recurrent nets aur generative models me kaam aa sakta hai.
  • Output layer ka tip: classifier me output layer ke weights ko initialization ke time scale down karo (jaise 10 guna) — shuru me logits chhote rahenge, probabilities ek-doosre ke kareeb hongi, aur model shuru me overconfident nahi hoga.

Activation functions — ReLU se aage

  • Dying ReLU: ReLU ka problem hai ki kuch neurons mar jaate hain — unke weights aise tweak ho jaate hain ki ReLU ka input har training instance ke liye negative rehta hai, output hamesha 0, aur gradient 0 hone se wo kabhi update nahi hota. Bada learning rate isse badhata hai.
  • Leaky ReLU: max(alpha*z, z) — negative side par chhoti slope (alpha) hoti hai, isliye neurons kabhi poori tarah nahi marte. Alpha = 0.2 aksar 0.01 se behtar karta hai. Randomized version me alpha training me random hota hai; parametric version me alpha khud seekha jaata hai (bade datasets par behtar, chhote par overfitting ka risk).
  • ELU: negative side par exponential curve hoti hai — average output 0 ke kareeb rehta hai, dead neurons nahi hote, aur alpha = 1 ho to function har jagah smooth hota hai. Lekin exponential ki wajah se compute karne me ReLU se slow hai.
  • SELU: ELU ka scaled variant (lagbhag 1.05×, alpha lagbhag 1.67). Sirf dense layers wale MLP me, standardized inputs + sahi initialization ke saath, network self-normalize karta hai — har layer ka output mean 0 aur standard deviation 1 preserve karta hai. Lekin conditions sakht hain: L1/L2, batch-norm, layer-norm ya regular dropout use nahi kar sakte.
  • GELU, Swish, Mish: teeno ReLU ke smooth, nonconvex, nonmonotonic variants hain. GELU aksar sabse behtar karta hai; Swish (generalized form z*sigmoid(beta*z)) complex tasks ke liye accha default hai; Mish thoda aur behtar ho sakta hai lekin zyada compute maangta hai. GELU ka fast approximation z*sigmoid(1.702*z) hai.

Kaunsi activation chuno?

ReLU zyada tar tasks ke liye accha default hai — fast hai aur aksar sophisticated functions jitna hi accha hai. Complex tasks ke liye Swish behtar ho sakta hai, aur sabse complex ke liye trainable beta wala Swish. Low latency chahiye to leaky ReLU ya mobile ke liye Hardswish jaise simplified versions use karo.

Yaad rakho: Activation aur initialization ko alag-alag mat chuno — har activation ke liye uska matching initialization scale use karo, warna gradients phir unstable ho jayenge.
Poora code dekho — Weight initialization (Notebook 11, Ch 11)
python — Weight initialization — GitHub: https://github.com/ageron/handson-mlp/blob/main/11_training_deep_neural_networks.ipynb
import torch
import torch.nn as nn

layer = nn.Linear(40, 10)
layer.weight.data *= 6 ** 0.5  # [Name] init (or 3 ** 0.5 for [Name] init)
torch.zero_(layer.bias.data)

layer = nn.Linear(40, 10)
nn.init.kaiming_uniform_(layer.weight)
nn.init.zeros_(layer.bias)

def use_he_init(module):
    if isinstance(module, nn.Linear):
        nn.init.kaiming_uniform_(module.weight)
        nn.init.zeros_(module.bias)

model = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(50, 40), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(40, 1), nn.ReLU())
model.apply(use_he_init)

model = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(50, 40), nn.LeakyReLU(negative_slope=0.2))
model.apply(use_he_init)

Poora code dekho — SELU (Notebook 11, Ch 11)
python — SELU — GitHub: https://github.com/ageron/handson-mlp/blob/main/11_training_deep_neural_networks.ipynb
# extra code – this cell generates Figure 11–3

from scipy.special import erfc

# alpha and scale to self normalize with mean 0 and standard deviation 1
# (see equation 14 in the paper):
alpha_0_1 = -np.sqrt(2 / np.pi) / (erfc(1 / np.sqrt(2)) * np.exp(1 / 2) - 1)
scale_0_1 = (
    (1 - erfc(1 / np.sqrt(2)) * np.sqrt(np.e))
    * np.sqrt(2 * np.pi)
    * (
        2 * erfc(np.sqrt(2)) * np.e ** 2
        + np.pi * erfc(1 / np.sqrt(2)) ** 2 * np.e
        - 2 * (2 + np.pi) * erfc(1 / np.sqrt(2)) * np.sqrt(np.e)
        + np.pi
        + 2
    ) ** (-1 / 2)
)

def elu(z, alpha=1):
    return np.where(z < 0, alpha * (np.exp(z) - 1), z)

def selu(z, scale=scale_0_1, alpha=alpha_0_1):
    return scale * elu(z, alpha)

z = np.linspace(-5, 5, 200)
plt.plot(z, elu(z), "b-", linewidth=2, label=r"ELU$_\alpha(z) = \alpha (e^z - 1)$ if $z < 0$, else $z$")
plt.plot(z, selu(z), "r--", linewidth=2, label=r"SELU$(z) = 1.05 \, $ELU$_{1.67}(z)$")
plt.plot([-5, 5], [0, 0], 'k-')
plt.plot([-5, 5], [-1, -1], 'k:', linewidth=2)
plt.plot([-5, 5], [-1.758, -1.758], 'k:', linewidth=2)
plt.plot([0, 0], [-2.2, 3.2], 'k-')
plt.grid(True)
plt.axis([-5, 5, -2.2, 3.2])
plt.xlabel("$z$")
plt.gca().set_aspect("equal")
plt.legend()

plt.show()

torch.manual_seed(42)
model = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(50, 40), nn.SELU())
nn.init.kaiming_uniform_(model[0].weight)
model(torch.rand(2, 50)).shape
Poora code dekho — GELU, Swish, SwiGLU, Mish, ReLU² (Notebook 11, Ch 11)
python — GELU, Swish, SwiGLU, Mish, ReLU² — GitHub: https://github.com/ageron/handson-mlp/blob/main/11_training_deep_neural_networks.ipynb
# extra code – this cell generates Figure 11–4

def swish(z, beta=1):
    return z * sigmoid(beta * z)

def approx_gelu(z):
    return swish(z, beta=1.702)

def softplus(z):
    return np.log(1 + np.exp(z))

def mish(z):
    return z * np.tanh(softplus(z))

def relu_squared(z):
    return np.maximum(0, z)**2

z = np.linspace(-4, 2, 50)

beta = 0.6
plt.plot(z, approx_gelu(z), "b-", linewidth=2,
         label=r"GELU$(z) = z\,\Phi(z)$")
plt.plot(z, swish(z), "r--", linewidth=2,
         label=r"Swish$(z) = z\,\sigma(z)$")
plt.plot(z, swish(z, beta), "r:", linewidth=2,
         label=fr"Swish$_{{\beta={beta}}}(z)=z\,\sigma({beta}\,z)$")
plt.plot(z, mish(z), "k-.", linewidth=2,
         label=fr"Mish$(z) = z\,\tanh($softplus$(z))$")
plt.plot(z, relu_squared(z), "g.-", linewidth=1,
         label=fr"ReLU²$(z) = (\max(0, z))^2$")
plt.plot([-4, 2], [0, 0], 'k-')
plt.plot([0, 0], [-2.2, 3.2], 'k-')
plt.grid(True)
plt.axis([-4, 2, -1, 2])
plt.gca().set_aspect("equal")
plt.xlabel("$z$")
plt.legend(loc="upper left")

plt.show()

class SwiGLU(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, beta=1.0):
        super().__init__()
        self.beta = beta

    def forward(self, x):
        z1, z2 = x.chunk(2, dim=-1)
        param_swish = z1 * torch.sigmoid(self.beta * z1)
        return param_swish * z2

torch.manual_seed(42)
model = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(50, 2 * 40), SwiGLU(beta=0.2))
nn.init.kaiming_uniform_(model[0].weight)
model(torch.rand(2, 50)).shape

import torch.nn.functional as F

class ReLU2(nn.Module):
    def forward(self, x):
        return F.relu(x).square()

torch.manual_seed(42)
model = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(50, 40), ReLU2())
nn.init.kaiming_uniform_(model[0].weight)
model(torch.rand(2, 50)).shape

11.3Chapter 11 · Training Deep Neural Networks

Batch Normalization aur Gradient Clipping

Sahi initialization aur activation training ke shuru me gradients ko stable rakhte hain, lekin training ke dauraan problem wapas aa sakti hai. Batch normalization (BN) iska ek powerful ilaaj hai — aur jab BN mushkil ho (jaise recurrent nets me), to gradient clipping kaam aata hai.

Batch normalization kaise kaam karta hai?

Har hidden layer ki activation se pehle ya baad me ek operation add karo jo inputs ko zero-center aur normalize kare, phir do naye parameter vectors se unhe scale aur shift kare — gamma (scale) aur beta (shift). Matlab model khud seekhta hai ki har layer ke inputs ka optimal scale aur mean kya hona chahiye.

  • Training me: mean aur standard deviation current mini-batch se compute hote hain (isliye naam batch normalization). Ek chhota smoothing term epsilon (aksar 10^-5) division-by-zero se bachata hai.
  • Test time par: batch statistics use nahi ho sakte — single instance par predict karna ho to batch hi nahi hoti. Isliye training ke dauraan moving average se final mean aur variance estimate kiye jaate hain, aur model.eval() ke baad wahi use hote hain.
  • PyTorch me: nn.BatchNorm1d(num_features) — pehli layer ke roop me use karo to StandardScaler ki zaroorat khatam ho jaati hai. Iske parameters hain weight (gamma) aur bias (beta); buffers hain running_mean, running_var aur num_batches_tracked.
  • Fayde: vanishing gradients kam hote hain, saturating activations (tanh, sigmoid) bhi use ho sakti hain, weight initialization ki sensitivity kam hoti hai, bade learning rates use ho sakte hain, aur training bahut tez hoti hai — ek mashhoor experiment me same accuracy 14 guna kam training steps me mili. Bonus: BN regularizer ki tarah bhi kaam karta hai.
  • Placement: BN ko activation se pehle lagana chahiye ya baad me — is par debate hai, task par depend karta hai. Pehle lagao to pehle wali Linear layer ka bias hata sakte ho (bias=False), kyunki BN me pehle se ek bias hota hai.
  • Momentum: running averages update karne ka hyperparameter hai — default 0.1 hai, lekin chhote batches (32 ya 64) ke liye 0.01 ya 0.001 behtar hota hai. Savdhaan: PyTorch me BN momentum ka matlab ulta hai — ye current running mean ka weight hota hai, jabki optimizers me conventional matlab hota hai.
  • Dimensions: BatchNorm1d [batch, features] par, BatchNorm2d images [batch, channels, height, width] par (har channel ka ek mean/variance), aur BatchNorm3d 3D images par kaam karta hai.

Layer normalization — BN ka alternative

Layer normalization batch dimension ki jagah feature dimensions par normalize karta hai. Har instance ke liye alag se, on-the-fly statistics compute hote hain — isliye training aur testing me behavior same rehta hai, aur moving averages ki zaroorat nahi hoti. Ye recurrent nets me khaas taur par useful hai, aur aaj transformers aur diffusion models me bhi use hota hai. PyTorch me nn.LayerNorm([100, 200]) — normalize karne wale dimensions ki sizes deni hoti hain, jo inputs ke aakhiri dimensions hone chahiye.

Gradient clipping — exploding gradients ko roko

Gradient clipping me backprop ke dauraan gradients ko ek threshold se upar jaane nahi diya jaata. Ye khaas taur par recurrent nets me use hota hai, jahan batch norm tricky hai. loss.backward() ke turant baad call karo: nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), max_norm=1.0) gradient vector ka norm clip karta hai (orientation preserve rehti hai), jabki clip_grad_value_() har component ko alag se clip karta hai (orientation badal sakti hai, phir bhi practice me accha kaam karta hai). Kaunsa behtar hai, ye dataset par depend karta hai.

Yaad rakho: Batch norm ya dropout use kar rahe ho to model.train() aur model.eval() switch karna bhoolna sabse common galti hai — eval mode bhoolne par BN galat statistics use karega aur model kharab predict karega.
Poora code dekho — Batch normalization (Notebook 11, Ch 11)
python — Batch normalization — GitHub: https://github.com/ageron/handson-mlp/blob/main/11_training_deep_neural_networks.ipynb
torch.manual_seed(42)

model = nn.Sequential(
    nn.Flatten(),
    nn.BatchNorm1d(1 * 28 * 28),
    nn.Linear(1 * 28 * 28, 300),
    nn.ReLU(),
    nn.BatchNorm1d(300),
    nn.Linear(300, 100),
    nn.ReLU(),
    nn.BatchNorm1d(100),
    nn.Linear(100, 10)
)

dict(model[1].named_parameters()).keys()

dict(model[1].named_buffers()).keys()

torch.manual_seed(42)

model = nn.Sequential(
    nn.Flatten(),
    nn.Linear(1 * 28 * 28, 300, bias=False),
    nn.BatchNorm1d(300),
    nn.ReLU(),
    nn.Linear(300, 100, bias=False),
    nn.BatchNorm1d(100),
    nn.ReLU(),
    nn.Linear(100, 10)
)
Poora code dekho — Layer normalization (Notebook 11, Ch 11)
python — Layer normalization — GitHub: https://github.com/ageron/handson-mlp/blob/main/11_training_deep_neural_networks.ipynb
torch.manual_seed(42)

inputs = torch.randn(32, 3, 100, 200)  # a batch of random RGB images
layer_norm = nn.LayerNorm([100, 200])
result = layer_norm(inputs)  # normalizes over the last two dimensions

means = inputs.mean(dim=[2, 3], keepdim=True)
vars_ = inputs.var(dim=[2, 3], keepdim=True, unbiased=False)
stds = torch.sqrt(vars_ + layer_norm.eps)
result2 = layer_norm.weight * (inputs - means) / stds + layer_norm.bias
assert torch.allclose(result, result2)

layer_norm = nn.LayerNorm([3, 100, 200])
result = layer_norm(inputs)  # normalizes over the last three dimensions
SOURCESource: Hands-On Machine Learning with Scikit-Learn and PyTorch, O'Reilly, Chapter 11 — Training Deep Neural Networks

11.4Chapter 11 · Training Deep Neural Networks

Reusing Pretrained Layers, Optimizers aur Learning Rate Scheduling

Bada DNN scratch se train karna hamesha sahi nahi hota. Pehle dekho kya koi existing network tumhare jaisa kaam kar raha hai — uski layers reuse karne se training tez hoti hai aur kam data chahiye hota hai. Aur jab training slow ho, to tez optimizer aur smart learning rate schedule se bada farq padta hai.

Transfer learning — pretrained layers reuse karo

  • Idea: 100 categories classify karne wale model ki layers lekar naye task (jaise specific vehicles classify karna) me use karo. Output layer hamesha replace karo — wo naye task ke liye useful nahi hoti aur outputs ki sankhya bhi galat ho sakti hai. Upper hidden layers lower layers se kam useful hoti hain, kyunki high-level features naye task ke liye alag ho sakte hain.
  • Freeze phir unfreeze: pehle reused layers ko freeze karo (requires_grad = False), nayi output layer ko kuch epochs train hone do — warna uske bade gradients reused weights ko kharab kar denge. Phir ek-do top hidden layers unfreeze karo, learning rate kam karke fine-tune karo. Jitna zyada training data, utni zyada layers unfreeze kar sakte ho.
  • PyTorch example: Fashion MNIST par 8 classes wala model A lekar sirf T-shirt/top vs Pullover ka binary classifier banaya — sirf 20 labeled images se scratch model ko 71.6% accuracy mili, transfer learning se 92.5% mili. Lekin savdhaan: ye example cherry-picked tha — chhote dense networks me transfer learning aksar itna accha nahi karta, kyunki wo kam aur bahut specific patterns seekhte hain. Ye technique deep convolutional networks aur transformer architectures me sabse behtar kaam karti hai.
  • Input size ka dhyaan: naye task ki images ka size alag ho to resize karna padega. Transfer learning tabhi behtar kaam karta hai jab inputs ke low-level features similar hon — mobile photos par trained net satellite ya medical images me madad nahi karega.

Unsupervised pretraining aur auxiliary tasks

  • Unsupervised pretraining: labeled data kam ho lekin unlabeled data bahut ho, to pehle autoencoder jaise unsupervised model train karo, phir uski lower layers reuse karke apne task ki output layer jodo aur labeled data se fine-tune karo. Purane time me layer-by-layer greedy pretraining hoti thi; aaj poora unsupervised model ek shot me train hota hai.
  • Auxiliary task: aisi task par pehle train karo jiske liye labeled data aasani se mile — jaise face recognition ke liye pehle ye seekhao ki do photos me wahi vyakti hai ya nahi. NLP me words ko mask karke missing word predict karwana — yehi self-supervised learning hai, aur large language models isi tarah train aur fine-tune hote hain.

Faster optimizers

  • Momentum: gradient ko speed ki jagah acceleration ki tarah use karo — momentum vector m past gradients ko yaad rakhta hai (coefficient beta, aksar 0.9). Gentle slope par bhi speed badhti jaati hai, plateaus se tez nikalte hain, aur elongated valleys me gradient descent se bahut tez hote hain. PyTorch: torch.optim.SGD(model.parameters(), momentum=0.9, lr=0.05).
  • Look-ahead momentum: gradient ko current position par nahi, momentum ki direction me thoda aage jaakar measure karo — update optimum ke kareeb aata hai aur oscillations kam hote hain. PyTorch me SGD optimizer ka look-ahead momentum option on karke use karo.
  • AdaGrad: har parameter ke liye adaptive learning rate — steep dimensions me learning rate tez ghat-ta hai. Lekin neural nets me ye aksar bahut jaldi ruk jaata hai, global optimum tak pahunchne se pehle hi. Deep nets ke liye use mat karo.
  • RMSProp: AdaGrad ka fix — sirf recent gradients accumulate karta hai (exponential decay, alpha aksar 0.9). AdaGrad se lagbhag hamesha behtar hai.
  • Adam: momentum + RMSProp ka combination — past gradients ka average (first moment) aur past squared gradients ka average (second moment) dono track karta hai, aur shuru me bias correction karta hai. Defaults: betas (0.9, 0.999), learning rate aksar 0.001 hi kaafi hota hai. PyTorch: torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), betas=(0.9, 0.999), lr=0.05).
  • Variants: AdaMax (L2 norm ki jagah max norm use karta hai, zyada stable ho sakta hai), NAdam (Adam + look-ahead trick, aksar thoda tez), AdamW (weight decay ko Adam ke saath sahi tareeke se jodta hai — Adam + L2 regularization utna generalize nahi karta). Savdhaan: adaptive optimizers kabhi-kabhi aise solutions dete hain jo generalize nahi karte — tab look-ahead momentum wala SGD try karo.

Learning rate scheduling

  • Basic idea: shuru me kaafi high learning rate se tez progress karo, ant me kam karke fine-tune karo. Constant rate se ye behtar hai.
  • Exponential: har epoch rate ko gamma se multiply karo (jaise 0.9 — 10 epochs baad 35%, 20 epochs baad 12%). ExponentialLR(optimizer, gamma=0.9), har epoch ke ant me scheduler.step() karo.
  • Cosine annealing: cosine curve se max se min tak jao — rate zyada der tak high rehta hai, ant me min ke kareeb aata hai. CosineAnnealingLR(optimizer, T_max=20, eta_min=0.001).
  • Performance scheduling: validation metric (jaise validation loss) improve hona band ho to rate ko factor se multiply karo. ReduceLROnPlateau(optimizer, mode="max", patience=2, factor=0.1) — har epoch metric compute karke scheduler.step(val_metric) karo.
  • Warmup: shuru me rate ko 0 ke kareeb se gradually max tak badhao (jaise LinearLR se 3 epochs me 10% se 100%) — sensitive models ya bade batches me shuru ki instability se bachata hai. Warmup ke dauraan doosre schedulers ko deactivate rakho.
  • Warm restarts aur 1cycle: cosine annealing ko baar-baar repeat karo (T_max har round double karo) to local optima aur plateaus se nikal sakte ho — CosineAnnealingWarmRestarts. 1cycle schedule warmup + cooldown ko ek cycle me karta hai aur super-convergence de sakta hai — OneCycleLR. Agar confuse ho to 1cycle accha default hai; shuru me instability ho to warmup add karo; plateaus par atak rahe ho to warm restarts try karo.
Yaad rakho: Optimizer aur schedule chunne se pehle initialization, activation aur normalization sahi karo — ye chaar cheezein (initialization, activation, norm, pretrained reuse) hi sabse bada speedup deti hain.

python — PyTorch se transfer learning — GitHub: https://github.com/ageron/handson-mlp/blob/main/11_training_deep_neural_networks.ipynb
from torch.utils.data import TensorDataset, DataLoader
from sklearn.datasets import fetch_openml

fashion_mnist = fetch_openml(name="Fashion-MNIST", as_frame=False)
X = torch.FloatTensor(fashion_mnist.data.reshape(-1, 1, 28, 28) / 255.)
y = torch.from_numpy(fashion_mnist.target.astype(int))
in_B = (y == 0) | (y == 2)  # Pullover or T-shirt/top
X_A, y_A = X[~in_B], y[~in_B]
y_A = torch.maximum(y_A - 2, torch.tensor(0))  # [1,3,4,5,6,7,8,9] => [0,..,7]
X_B, y_B = X[in_B], (y[in_B] == 2).to(dtype=torch.float32).view(-1, 1)

train_set_A = TensorDataset(X_A[:-7_000], y_A[:-7000])
valid_set_A = TensorDataset(X_A[-7_000:-5000], y_A[-7000:-5000])
test_set_A = TensorDataset(X_A[-5_000:], y_A[-5000:])
train_set_B = TensorDataset(X_B[:20], y_B[:20])
valid_set_B = TensorDataset(X_B[20:5000], y_B[20:5000])
test_set_B = TensorDataset(X_B[5_000:], y_B[5000:])

train_loader_A = DataLoader(train_set_A, batch_size=32, shuffle=True)
valid_loader_A = DataLoader(valid_set_A, batch_size=32)
test_loader_A = DataLoader(test_set_A, batch_size=32)
train_loader_B = DataLoader(train_set_B, batch_size=32, shuffle=True)
valid_loader_B = DataLoader(valid_set_B, batch_size=32)
test_loader_B = DataLoader(test_set_B, batch_size=32)

import torchmetrics

def evaluate_tm(model, data_loader, metric):
    model.eval()
    metric.reset()
    with torch.no_grad():
        for X_batch, y_batch in data_loader:
            X_batch, y_batch = X_batch.to(device), y_batch.to(device)
            y_pred = model(X_batch)
            metric.update(y_pred, y_batch)
    return metric.compute()

def train(model, optimizer, loss_fn, metric, train_loader, valid_loader,
          n_epochs):
    history = {"train_losses": [], "train_metrics": [], "valid_metrics": []}
    for epoch in range(n_epochs):
        total_loss = 0.0
        metric.reset()
        model.train()
        for X_batch, y_batch in train_loader:
            X_batch, y_batch = X_batch.to(device), y_batch.to(device)
            y_pred = model(X_batch)
            loss = loss_fn(y_pred, y_batch)
            total_loss += loss.item()
            loss.backward()
            # Uncomment to activate gradient clipping:
            #nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), max_norm=1.0)
            optimizer.step()
            optimizer.zero_grad()
            metric.update(y_pred, y_batch)
        history["train_losses"].append(total_loss / len(train_loader))
        history["train_metrics"].append(metric.compute().item())
        history["valid_metrics"].append(
            evaluate_tm(model, valid_loader, metric).item())
        print(f"Epoch {epoch + 1}/{n_epochs}, "
              f"train loss: {history['train_losses'][-1]:.4f}, "
              f"train metric: {history['train_metrics'][-1]:.4f}, "
              f"valid metric: {history['valid_metrics'][-1]:.4f}")
    return history

torch.manual_seed(42)

model_A = nn.Sequential(
    nn.Flatten(),
    nn.Linear(28 * 28, 100),
    nn.ReLU(),
    nn.Linear(100, 100),
    nn.ReLU(),
    nn.Linear(100, 100),
    nn.ReLU(),
    nn.Linear(100, 8)
)
model_A = model_A.to(device)

model_A.apply(use_he_init)

n_epochs = 20
optimizer = torch.optim.SGD(model_A.parameters(), lr=0.005)
xentropy = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
accuracy = torchmetrics.Accuracy(task="multiclass", num_classes=8).to(device)
history_A = train(model_A, optimizer, xentropy, accuracy,
                  train_loader_A, valid_loader_A, n_epochs)

torch.manual_seed(9)

model_B = nn.Sequential(
    nn.Flatten(),
    nn.Linear(28 * 28, 100),
    nn.ReLU(),
    nn.Linear(100, 100),
    nn.ReLU(),
    nn.Linear(100, 100),
    nn.ReLU(),
    nn.Linear(100, 1)

model_B.apply(use_he_init)

n_epochs = 20

xentropy = nn.BCEWithLogitsLoss()
accuracy = torchmetrics.Accuracy(task="binary").to(device)

# extra code – a little function to test an optimizer on Fashion MNIST

train_set = TensorDataset(X[:55_000], y[:55_000])
valid_set = TensorDataset(X[55_000:60_000], y[55_000:60_000])
test_set = TensorDataset(X[60_000:], y[60_000:])

def build_model(seed=42):
    torch.manual_seed(seed)
    model = nn.Sequential(
        nn.Flatten(),
        nn.Linear(28 * 28, 100),
        nn.ReLU(),
        nn.Linear(100, 100),
        nn.ReLU(),
        nn.Linear(100, 100),
        nn.ReLU(),
        nn.Linear(100, 10)
    ).to(device)
    model.apply(use_he_init)
    return model

def test_optimizer(model, optimizer, n_epochs=10, batch_size=32):
    train_loader = DataLoader(train_set, batch_size=32, shuffle=True)
    valid_loader = DataLoader(valid_set, batch_size=32)
    test_loader = DataLoader(test_set, batch_size=32)
    xentropy = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
    accuracy = torchmetrics.Accuracy(task="multiclass", num_classes=10)
    history = train(model, optimizer, xentropy, accuracy.to(device),
                    train_loader, valid_loader, n_epochs)
    return history, evaluate_tm(model, test_loader, accuracy)

model = build_model()  # extra code
optimizer = torch.optim.SGD(model.parameters(), lr=0.05)
history_sgd, acc_sgd = test_optimizer(model, optimizer)  # extra code

model = build_model()  # extra code

def train_with_scheduler(model, optimizer, loss_fn, metric, train_loader,
                         valid_loader, n_epochs, scheduler):
    history = {"train_losses": [], "train_metrics": [], "valid_metrics": []}
    for epoch in range(n_epochs):
        losses = []
        metric.reset()
        for X_batch, y_batch in train_loader:
            model.train()
            X_batch, y_batch = X_batch.to(device), y_batch.to(device)
            y_pred = model(X_batch)
            loss = loss_fn(y_pred, y_batch)
            losses.append(loss.item())
            loss.backward()
            optimizer.step()
            optimizer.zero_grad()
            metric.update(y_pred, y_batch)
        history["train_losses"].append(np.mean(losses))
        history["train_metrics"].append(metric.compute().item())
        val_metric = evaluate_tm(model, valid_loader, metric).item()
        history["valid_metrics"].append(val_metric)
        print(f"Epoch {epoch + 1}/{n_epochs}, "
              f"train loss: {history['train_losses'][-1]:.4f}, "
              f"train metric: {history['train_metrics'][-1]:.4f}, "
              f"valid metric: {history['valid_metrics'][-1]:.4f}")
        if isinstance(scheduler, torch.optim.lr_scheduler.ReduceLROnPlateau):
            scheduler.step(val_metric)
        else:
            scheduler.step()
        print(f"Learning rate: {scheduler.get_last_lr()[0]:.5f}")
    return history

def test_scheduler(model, optimizer, scheduler, n_epochs=10, batch_size=32):
    train_loader = DataLoader(train_set, batch_size=32, shuffle=True)
    valid_loader = DataLoader(valid_set, batch_size=32)
    test_loader = DataLoader(test_set, batch_size=32)
    xentropy = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
    metric = torchmetrics.Accuracy(task="multiclass", num_classes=10).to(device)
    history = train_with_scheduler(
        model, optimizer, xentropy, metric, train_loader, valid_loader,
        n_epochs, scheduler)
    return history, evaluate_tm(model, test_loader, metric)

history_exp, acc_exp = test_scheduler(model, optimizer, exp_scheduler)  # extra code

# extra code
def train_with_warmup(model, optimizer, loss_fn, metric, train_loader,
                      valid_loader, n_epochs, warmup_scheduler, scheduler):
    history = {"train_losses": [], "train_metrics": [], "valid_metrics": []}
    for epoch in range(n_epochs):

        warmup_scheduler.step()

        # extra code
        losses = []
        metric.reset()

        for X_batch, y_batch in train_loader:

            # extra code
            model.train()
            X_batch, y_batch = X_batch.to(device), y_batch.to(device)
            y_pred = model(X_batch)
            loss = loss_fn(y_pred, y_batch)
            losses.append(loss.item())
            loss.backward()
            optimizer.step()
            optimizer.zero_grad()
            metric.update(y_pred, y_batch)
        history["train_losses"].append(np.mean(losses))
        history["train_metrics"].append(metric.compute().item())
        val_metric = evaluate_tm(model, valid_loader, metric).item()
        history["valid_metrics"].append(val_metric)
        print(f"Epoch {epoch + 1}/{n_epochs}, "
              f"train loss: {history['train_losses'][-1]:.4f}, "
              f"train metric: {history['train_metrics'][-1]:.4f}, "
              f"valid metric: {history['valid_metrics'][-1]:.4f}")

        if epoch >= 3:  # deactivate other scheduler(s) during warmup
            scheduler.step(val_metric)

        # extra code
        print(f"Learning rate: {scheduler.get_last_lr()[0]:.5f}")
    return history

def test_warmup_scheduler(model, optimizer, warmup_scheduler, scheduler,
                          n_epochs=10, batch_size=32):
    train_loader = DataLoader(train_set, batch_size=32, shuffle=True)
    valid_loader = DataLoader(valid_set, batch_size=32)
    test_loader = DataLoader(test_set, batch_size=32)

    history = train_with_warmup(
        model, optimizer, xentropy, metric, train_loader, valid_loader,
        n_epochs, warmup_scheduler, scheduler)
    return history, evaluate_tm(model, test_loader, metric)

11.5Chapter 11 · Training Deep Neural Networks

Regularization — Dropout aur Weight Decay

Deep networks me hazaaron se arabon parameters hote hain — itni freedom se wo training set ko ratne lagte hain. Early stopping aur batch-norm pehle se hi regularizers ki tarah kaam karte hain, lekin is section me chaar aur popular techniques hain: L1/L2 regularization, dropout, MC dropout aur max-norm regularization.

L1 aur L2 regularization (weight decay)

  • SGD ke saath: L2 regularization weight decay ke barabar hoti hai — bas optimizer me weight_decay=1e-4 set karo: torch.optim.SGD(model.parameters(), lr=0.05, weight_decay=1e-4).
  • Adam ke saath: AdamW use karo aur weight_decay set karo — Adam + L2 utna accha generalize nahi karta, AdamW isse fix karta hai.
  • Selective regularization: weight decay har parameter par lagta hai — bias aur batch-norm parameters par bhi, jo regularization me madad nahi karte. Sirf weights par lagana ho to loss me manually L2 term jodo (loss = main_loss + 1e-4 * l2_loss), ya optimizer ke parameter groups use karo — ek group weights ke liye (weight_decay ke saath), doosra bias/BN ke liye (bina weight_decay).
  • L1 regularization: PyTorch me iska helper nahi hai — manually karo: l1_loss = sum(param.abs().sum() ...) aur main loss me jodo. L1 sparse models banata hai (kai weights zero ho jaate hain).
  • Sparse models: training ke baad chhote weights ko zero karo (torch.nn.prune.l1_unstructured()), ya poore neurons/channels ko hatao (ln_structured()). Sparse model runtime par tez aur chhota hota hai.

Dropout — har step par random neurons band karo

Har training step par har neuron (output neurons ko chhodkar) ki probability p hoti hai ki wo temporarily drop ho jaaye — is step me wo bilkul ignore hoga, agle step me wapas aa sakta hai. Dropout rate aksar 10%–50% hota hai: recurrent nets me 20%–30%, convolutional nets me 40%–50% ke kareeb.

  • Kyun kaam karta hai: neurons ek-doosre par depend nahi kar sakte — har neuron ko khud useful hona padta hai aur har input par dhyaan dena padta hai. Har step par ek alag network train hota hai (2^N possible networks) — final model in sabka ensemble average jaisa hota hai. Isse 1%–2% accuracy boost milta hai, jo 95% accuracy par error rate ko lagbhag 40% kam kar deta hai.
  • Keep probability scaling: training me sirf (1 - p) neurons active hote hain, isliye training ke dauraan bache inputs ko (1 - p) se divide karo — warna test time par neurons ko 4 guna zyada inputs milenge.
  • PyTorch me: nn.Dropout(p=0.2) — training me drop karta hai, evaluation me kuch nahi karta. Top hidden layers par dropout zyada fayda deta hai; output neurons ko kabhi drop mat karo. Overfitting ho to rate badhao, underfitting ho to ghatao. Dropout convergence ko slow karta hai, lekin tuned hone par behtar model deta hai.
  • SELU networks ke liye: regular dropout self-normalization tod deta hai — isliye nn.AlphaDropout use karo, jo inputs ka mean aur standard deviation preserve karta hai.

MC dropout — uncertainty bhi measure karo

MC dropout me dropout evaluation ke time bhi active rehta hai. Ek hi image ki 100 copies banao, har par predict karo, aur probabilities ka mean lo — ye original model se behtar predictions deta hai aur uncertainty bhi batata hai. Implementation: model.eval() karo, phir saare Dropout layers ko wapas train() mode me daalo, phir repeat_interleave(100) se repeated batch banao aur mean lo. Standard deviation dekhkar pata chalta hai ki model kitna sure hai — jaise 97% probability par 0.06 std matlab model asal me keh raha hai "90% se upar guess kar raha hoon". Risk-sensitive systems (medical, financial) me high probability + low std wali predictions par hi bharosa karo. Pehle probabilities ka mean lo, phir convert karo — ulta karne se overconfident model milta hai.

Max-norm regularization

Har neuron ke incoming weights ka L2 norm ek limit r se zyada nahi hona chahiye: ||w||2 ≤ r. r kam karo to regularization badhta hai. Ye loss term se nahi, har training step ke baad weights ko rescale karke implement hota hai. Isse unstable gradients me bhi madad milti hai (agar batch-norm ya layer-norm use nahi kar rahe).

Default configuration — kahan se shuru karo?

  • General default: ReLU ke liye wali initialization; activation ReLU (shallow) ya Swish (deep); normalization none (shallow) ya batch-norm/layer-norm (deep); regularization early stopping + zaroorat ho to weight decay; optimizer look-ahead momentum ya AdamW; schedule performance scheduling ya 1cycle.
  • Self-normalizing net (sirf dense layers): SELU ke liye wali initialization; SELU activation; no normalization; regularization alpha dropout; optimizer look-ahead momentum; schedule performance scheduling ya 1cycle. Input features normalize karna mat bhoolo.
  • Exceptions: sparse model chahiye to L1 use karo; low-latency chahiye to kam layers, fast activation (ReLU, leaky ReLU, Hardswish), aur BN/LN ko training ke baad previous layer me fold karo; risk-sensitive app ho to MC dropout use karo.
Yaad rakho: Dropout ya batch-norm use kar rahe ho to training loss aur validation loss ki tulna misleading ho sakti hai — training loss ko dropout ke bina (evaluation mode me) measure karo.

n_epochs = 3
train_loader = DataLoader(train_set, batch_size=32, shuffle=True)
loss_fn = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()

model = build_model()  # extra code
optimizer = torch.optim.SGD(model.parameters(), lr=0.05)
params_to_regularize = [
    param for name, param in model.named_parameters()
    if not "bias" in name and not "bn" in name]
for epoch in range(n_epochs):
    total_loss = 0.0
    total_l2_loss = 0.0
    for X_batch, y_batch in train_loader:
        model.train()
        X_batch, y_batch = X_batch.to(device), y_batch.to(device)
        y_pred = model(X_batch)
        main_loss = loss_fn(y_pred, y_batch)
        l2_loss = sum(param.pow(2.0).sum() for param in params_to_regularize)
        loss = main_loss + 1e-4 * l2_loss
        total_loss += loss.item()
        total_l2_loss += l2_loss.item()
        loss.backward()
        optimizer.step()
        optimizer.zero_grad()
    print(f"Epoch {epoch + 1}/{n_epochs}"
          f" – l2 loss: {total_l2_loss / len(train_loader):.3f}"
          f" – loss: {total_loss / len(train_loader):.3f}")

class McDropout(nn.Dropout):
    def forward(self, input):
        return F.dropout(input, self.p, training=True)

def mean_prediction(model, X, n_repeats):
    X_new_repeated = X_new.repeat_interleave(n_repeats, dim=0)
    y_logits = model(X_new_repeated)
    y_logits_all = y_logits.reshape(X.shape[0], n_repeats, *y_logits.shape[1:])
    y_probas_all = torch.nn.functional.softmax(y_logits_all, dim=-1)
    return y_probas_all.mean(dim=1)

with torch.no_grad():
  y_mean_pred = mean_prediction(model, X_new, 100)

y_mean_pred.round(decimals=2)

python — Max-norm regularization — GitHub: https://github.com/ageron/handson-mlp/blob/main/11_training_deep_neural_networks.ipynb
def apply_max_norm(model, max_norm=2, epsilon=1e-8, dim=1):
    with torch.no_grad():
        for name, param in model.named_parameters():
            if 'bias' not in name:
                actual_norm = param.norm(p=2, dim=dim, keepdim=True)
                target_norm = torch.clamp(actual_norm, 0, max_norm)
                param *= target_norm / (epsilon + actual_norm)

        loss.backward()

import torchvision
import torchvision.transforms.v2 as T

toTensor = T.Compose([T.ToImage(), T.ToDtype(torch.float32, scale=True)])
train_and_valid_set = torchvision.datasets.CIFAR10(
    root="datasets", train=True, download=True, transform=toTensor)
test_set = torchvision.datasets.CIFAR10(
    root="datasets", train=False, download=True, transform=toTensor)

torch.manual_seed(42)
train_set, valid_set = torch.utils.data.random_split(
    train_and_valid_set, [45_000, 5_000])

batch_size = 128
train_loader = DataLoader(train_set, batch_size=batch_size)
valid_loader = DataLoader(valid_set, batch_size=batch_size)
test_loader = DataLoader(test_set, batch_size=batch_size)

def use_he_init(module):
    if isinstance(module, nn.Linear):
        nn.init.kaiming_uniform_(module.weight)
        nn.init.zeros_(module.bias)

def build_deep_model(n_hidden, n_neurons, n_inputs, n_outputs):
    layers = [nn.Flatten(), nn.Linear(n_inputs, n_neurons), nn.SiLU()]
    for _ in range(n_hidden - 1):
        layers += [nn.Linear(n_neurons, n_neurons), nn.SiLU()]

    layers += [nn.Linear(n_neurons, n_outputs)]
    model = torch.nn.Sequential(*layers)
    model.apply(use_he_init)
    return model

torch.manual_seed(42)
model = build_deep_model(
    n_hidden=20, n_neurons=100, n_inputs=3 * 32 * 32, n_outputs=10
).to(device)

import time

def train_with_early_stopping(model, optimizer, loss_fn, metric, train_loader,
                              valid_loader, n_epochs, patience=10,
                              checkpoint_path=None, scheduler=None):
    checkpoint_path = checkpoint_path or "my_checkpoint.pt"
    history = {"train_losses": [], "train_metrics": [], "valid_metrics": []}
    best_metric = 0.0
    patience_counter = 0
    for epoch in range(n_epochs):
        total_loss = 0.0
        metric.reset()
        model.train()
        t0 = time.time()
        for X_batch, y_batch in train_loader:
            X_batch, y_batch = X_batch.to(device), y_batch.to(device)
            y_pred = model(X_batch)
            loss = loss_fn(y_pred, y_batch)
            total_loss += loss.item()
            loss.backward()
            optimizer.step()
            optimizer.zero_grad()
            metric.update(y_pred, y_batch)

        train_metric = metric.compute().item()
        valid_metric = evaluate_tm(model, valid_loader, metric).item()
        if valid_metric > best_metric:
            torch.save(model.state_dict(), checkpoint_path)
            best_metric = valid_metric
            best = " (best)"
            patience_counter = 0
        else:
            patience_counter += 1
            best = ""

        t1 = time.time()
        history["train_losses"].append(total_loss / len(train_loader))
        history["train_metrics"].append(train_metric)
        history["valid_metrics"].append(valid_metric)
        print(f"Epoch {epoch + 1}/{n_epochs}, "
              f"train loss: {history['train_losses'][-1]:.4f}, "
              f"train metric: {history['train_metrics'][-1]:.4f}, "
              f"valid metric: {history['valid_metrics'][-1]:.4f}{best}"
              f" in {t1 - t0:.1f}s"
        )
        if scheduler is not None:
            scheduler.step()
        if patience_counter >= patience:
            print("Early stopping!")
            break

    model.load_state_dict(torch.load(checkpoint_path))
    return history

optimizer = torch.optim.NAdam(model.parameters(), lr=2e-3)
criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
accuracy = torchmetrics.Accuracy(task="multiclass", num_classes=10).to(device)

n_epochs = 100
history = train_with_early_stopping(model, optimizer, criterion, accuracy,
                                    train_loader, valid_loader, n_epochs)

def build_deep_model_with_batch_norm(n_hidden, n_neurons, n_inputs, n_outputs):
    layers = [nn.Flatten(), nn.Linear(n_inputs, n_neurons),
              nn.BatchNorm1d(n_neurons), nn.SiLU()]
    for _ in range(n_hidden - 1):
        layers += [nn.Linear(n_neurons, n_neurons),
                   nn.BatchNorm1d(n_neurons), nn.SiLU()]

    layers += [nn.Linear(n_neurons, n_outputs)]
    model = torch.nn.Sequential(*layers)
    model.apply(use_he_init)
    return model

class Standardize(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, sample):
        super().__init__()
        flat = torch.flatten(sample, start_dim=1)
        mean = flat.mean(dim=0, keepdim=True)
        std = flat.std(dim=0, keepdim=True)
        self.register_buffer("mean", mean)
        self.register_buffer("std", std)

    def forward(self, x):
        return (x - self.mean) / self.std

all_images = torch.stack([img for img, _ in train_set])
standardize = Standardize(all_images)

def use_lecun_init(module):
    if isinstance(module, nn.Linear):
        nn.init.kaiming_normal_(module.weight, mode="fan_in",
                                nonlinearity="linear")
        nn.init.zeros_(module.bias)

def build_deep_model_with_selu(n_hidden, n_neurons, n_inputs, n_outputs):
    layers = [nn.Flatten(), standardize,
              nn.Linear(n_inputs, n_neurons), nn.SELU()]
    for _ in range(n_hidden - 1):
        layers += [nn.Linear(n_neurons, n_neurons), nn.SELU()]

    layers += [nn.Linear(n_neurons, n_outputs)]
    model = torch.nn.Sequential(*layers)
    model.apply(use_lecun_init)
    return model

torch.manual_seed(42)
model = build_deep_model_with_selu(
    n_hidden=20, n_neurons=100, n_inputs=3 * 32 * 32, n_outputs=10
).to(device)

optimizer = torch.optim.SGD(model.parameters(), lr=1e-3)
criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
accuracy = torchmetrics.Accuracy(task="multiclass", num_classes=10).to(device)

n_epochs = 100
history = train_with_early_stopping(model, optimizer, criterion, accuracy,
                                    train_loader, valid_loader, n_epochs)

def build_deep_model_with_alpha_dropout(n_hidden, n_neurons, n_inputs,
                                        n_outputs, dropout_rate):
    layers = [nn.Flatten(), standardize,
              nn.Linear(n_inputs, n_neurons), nn.SELU(),
              nn.AlphaDropout(dropout_rate)]
    for _ in range(n_hidden - 1):
        layers += [nn.Linear(n_neurons, n_neurons), nn.SELU(),
                   nn.AlphaDropout(dropout_rate)]

    layers += [nn.Linear(n_neurons, n_outputs)]
    model = torch.nn.Sequential(*layers)
    model.apply(use_lecun_init)
    return model

    n_hidden=20, n_neurons=100, n_inputs=3 * 32 * 32, n_outputs=10,
    dropout_rate=0.1

Chapters 9–11 se kya pata chalta hai

  • Batch-norm CNNs me standard hai: batch normalization khaas taur par deep convolutional networks me bahut use hota hai — itna ki architecture diagrams me ise aksar dikhaya bhi nahi jaata, ye assume kar liya jaata hai ki har layer ke baad BN hai.

Processing Sequences Using RNNs and CNNs

Yaad rakho: Ye chapter is Second Early Release PDF me nahi hai — ye overview book ke cross-references se banaya gaya hai.

Chapter 13 ka topic hai sequences ko process karna — recurrent neural networks (RNNs) aur CNNs se. Book ke Brief Table of Contents me is chapter ka naam "Processing Sequences Using RNNS and CNNs" diya hai, aur is release me ye unavailable mark hai.

Chapters 9–11 se kya pata chalta hai

  • Exploding gradients RNNs me: Chapter 11 kehta hai ki exploding gradients problem recurrent neural networks me sabse zyada dikhti hai.
  • Batch-norm RNNs me tricky hai: Chapter 11 me gradient clipping ko isliye introduce kiya gaya hai kyunki recurrent nets me batch-norm use karna mushkil hota hai — isliye wahan gradient clipping zyada use hoti hai.
  • Layer-norm RNNs ke liye aayi thi: layer normalization shuru me khaas taur par recurrent nets par apply ki gayi thi, kyunki ye har instance ke liye alag se kaam karti hai aur training/testing me same behave karti hai.
  • Sequences ka data format: PyTorch me sequences ke batches [batch_size, sequence_length, num_features] shape me hote hain — jaise 32 trajectories, har ek me 100 points, to shape [32, 100, 3] hoti hai.

The Transformer Revolution

Yaad rakho: Ye chapter is Second Early Release PDF me nahi hai — ye overview book ke cross-references se banaya gaya hai.

Chapter 15 ka topic hai Transformer architecture — jo 2017 me aaya aur deep learning me game changer ban gaya. Book ke Brief Table of Contents me is chapter ka naam "The Transformer Revolution" diya hai, aur is release me ye unavailable mark hai.

Chapters 9–11 se kya pata chalta hai

  • Ek architecture, har tarah ka data: Transformer text, images aur audio — sab process aur generate kar sakta hai, pehle ki zyada specialized architectures se alag. Ye robotics se lekar protein folding tak kai tasks me accha karta hai.
  • Scale aur foundation models: Transformer acche se scale hota hai, isliye bahut bade foundation models train kiye ja sake jo kai tasks me reuse hote hain — thodi fine-tuning se (transfer learning) ya sirf sahi prompt dekar (in-context learning, few-shot learning, chain-of-thought prompting).
  • ReLU ka exception: ReLU zyada tar architectures ka default hai — transformers ko chhodkar, jahan koi doosri activation use hoti hai.
  • Transfer learning transformers me: Chapter 11 kehta hai ki transfer learning transformer architectures ke saath sabse behtar kaam karta hai.

Train/Test Split Lab

Model ko train karne se pehle data ko train set aur test set me baantna padta hai. Test set woh data hota hai jise model ne training me kabhi dekha hi nahi — usi se pata chalta hai ki model naye data par kaisa perform karega. Neeche slider ghumao aur dekho ki stratified split aur random split me class proportion kaise badalta hai.

TRY ITTest size aur random state badlo — stratified vs random split compare karo
Result
Usool (Chapter 2): Stratified sampling me har category ka proportion train aur test dono set me poori population jaisa hi rehta hai. Random split me chhoti category test set se gayab bhi ho sakti hai, aur phir test score galat picture deta hai. Isliye jab data me categories hon, hamesha stratified split use karo.


SOURCESource: Hands-On Machine Learning with Scikit-Learn and PyTorch, O'Reilly, Chapter 2 — End-to-End Machine Learning Projects
